new.notes: Distress-for-rent exemption for goods consigned to a sales agent; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue present.
Married woman's separate-property/feme-sole-trader dispute against husband's judgment creditors; testimony that she 'kept boarders' is one of several passing income facts, not the litigated issue.

Innkeeper's tort liability for a guest's stolen property and contributory negligence from intoxication; concerns guest-property liability, not the legality, character, or regulation of letting/lodging.
Equity jurisdiction over an accounting for oil-well profits between alleged tenants in common; wholly unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.

new.cite: Craig v. First Presbyterian Church, 88 Pa. 42
new.notes: Statutory authority to remove remains from a church burial ground for a Sunday-school building; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: A city building inspector sought to enjoin an owner from continuing alterations of a back building into four separate tenement dwellings that lacked the open-space and street-width margins required for 'new' buildings under the Act of 1855. The court held the alterations did constitute a new building subject to the light-and-air requirements and ordered the rooms reopened to destroy their separate character, but held the statute gave courts no power to restrict the owner's right to let the building, once conforming, to one or several tenants as he chose.

quotes.text: we are unable to find any warrant in the statute to sustain the other part of the decree which restricts the appellant’s right to lease a part of his building separately, or permit it to be so occupied.
the right- of the owner to let it to one or to several tenants must remain unimpaired.
the right- of the owner to let it to one or to several tenants must remain unimpaired.

new.notes: Concerns subdivided tenement housing under building-safety regulation rather than short-term lodging per se, but squarely holds the owner's right to let separately is an incident of ownership that police-power building regulation cannot reach once the structure conforms to law.
Witness-competency/heirship title dispute under the Act of 1869; that Ann Harlan 'kept a boarding-house' before her marriage to Barber is background narrative, not the litigated issue.

new.cite: Kemble Coal & Iron Co. v. Scott, 90 Pa. 332
new.notes: Mining-royalty dispute turning on whether an ore-mining agreement was a lease or a mere license; the license-vs-lease analysis concerns mineral rights, not dwelling/room letting.
Competing land-warrant surveys and settlement-right title priority; wholly unrelated to lodging.
Riparian nuisance/dam-backwater dispute; the 'incident of ownership' language concerns natural flow of a stream, not letting of dwellings.
Married woman's title to farm products and livestock levied by her husband's creditors; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.
Trust/statute-of-limitations title dispute over an estate tail; unrelated to lodging.
Partition dispute among five congregations that jointly purchased a parsonage; concerns co-tenancy and dedicated charitable use, not letting of rooms for pay.

new.cite: Bishop O'Hara v. Grenawalt, 1 Law Times (N.S.) 171
new.court: Luzerne County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Property-tax exemption dispute for a Catholic school, convent, and parsonage as charitable/religious-use property; not a case about letting rooms or dwellings for pay.

new.court: Berks County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Married woman's title to land against her husband's judgment creditor; evidence that she 'kept boarders' is cited only to show her earnings still belonged to her husband absent a separate estate, not to characterize the boarding practice itself.

Ejectment procedure over joining a landlord as party defendant where a tenant-at-will occupied the land; a landlord-tenant fact pattern but the issue litigated is joinder practice, not the character of letting.

Oil-and-gas mining lease and partition-of-freehold dispute (whether a mining lessee is entitled to notice of an amicable partition among tenants in common). No lodging, boarding, or residential letting content.
Trover and conversion action by a former mining lessee against its landlord over trade fixtures forcibly withheld after entry under a forfeiture notice. No lodging/boarding content.

new.holding_summary: The Supreme Court affirmed the quarter sessions' refusal of retail liquor licenses to several hotel/tavern keepers, holding that on certiorari only the record (not the judge's stated reasons) is reviewable, and that a court may lawfully find a licensed house necessary for public accommodation while still concluding, on the petitions and remonstrances, that a liquor license is not necessary. The refusal of licenses to inns/taverns under the licensing statute was sustained.

quotes.text: The records in the cases before us are without fault, and as the facts cannot be brought .before us on appeal, we must affirm the certioraris, and dismiss the appeals.

“Our system of licensed inns and taverns,” says Judge Woodwakd, in Omit v. Com. 21 Pa. 434, “is founded in the just idea that it is the duty of every community to provide for the accommodation of strangers and travelers who come into their midst.
While such is the case, we, the associate judges, do not think that it is necessary to license a hotel to sell intoxicating liquors, and we therefore refuse this application.

new.notes: Innkeeper/hotel liquor-license regulation case; bears on ADVERSE file as licensing of a lodging/public-house business sustained under the licensing statute, though the direct dispute is over the liquor license rather than a lodging license per se.

Suit on a note given for a cask of brandy sold to a licensed innkeeper, plus a justice-of-the-peace jurisdictional-amount question. The innkeeper appears only as a liquor purchaser; no discussion of lodging, boarding, or letting of rooms.

new.holding_summary: The Supreme Court refused a writ of mandamus to compel a quarter sessions judge to grant a retail liquor license to a hotel keeper, holding that even though the hotel was conceded necessary for public accommodation and entertainment of strangers and travelers, the judge retained sound discretion to weigh remonstrances and could lawfully find that the license itself was not a matter of public necessity, so long as he did not simply substitute the remonstrants' will for his own judgment.

quotes.text: That the National Hotel for which said license was prayed, was then and still is a good hotel and necessary for the accommodation of the public and the entertainment of strangers and travelers.
In the view we take of the case, this was not an abuse of discretion.
We have decided repeatedly, in language too plain to be misunderstood, that the granting of a license to sell liquor by retail rests in the sound discretion of the court below.

new.notes: Companion doctrine to Leister's Appeal: sustains the licensing court's discretion to deny a hotel/innkeeper's liquor license notwithstanding the house's conceded necessity for lodging travelers, i.e., regulation of a lodging-adjacent commercial establishment upheld under the licensing statute.

Purely territorial/procedural question of whether a township liquor-sale prohibition act continued to apply to land later organized into a borough; certiorari record review only, with no discussion of hotel/lodging necessity or character of the business.
Spendthrift-trust/attachment-of-income case concerning whether a settlor can shield self-settled trust income from her own creditors. No connection to lodging, boarding, or letting.
Occupation tax on sellers of illustrated newspapers (Police News/Police Gazette); no connection to lodging, boarding, or letting of dwellings.
Sunday-closing law for liquor sales and municipal ordinance/charter conflict; no lodging or boarding house issue.
Occupation tax on railway ticket brokers ('scalpers'); police-power taxation case unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
Municipal court jurisdiction over unlawfully carrying a pistol; no bearing on lodging, boarding, or letting of dwellings.
City ordinance banning keeping of a stallion for breeding within city limits struck down as beyond nuisance-abatement power; unrelated to lodging/boarding.
Sunday-law prosecution of merchants for keeping place of business open; no lodging/boarding house issue.
Jurisdictional dispute over municipal court's power to try Sunday liquor-law violations; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

Conviction for permitting a 'disorderly house' where a prostitute plied her vocation for pay; this is a vice/prostitution offense under Penal Code arts. 359/361, not licensing or letting of a lodging/boarding house, so it does not bear on compensated occupancy of dwellings as contemplated by this corpus.
Municipal ordinance regulating hackmen/vehicle stops on city streets struck down as unreasonable; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

Trespass-to-try-title dispute over land patented to heirs, involving witness competency and cotenant conveyances; no lodging/boarding house issue despite selector match on general agency/conveyance language.
Adverse possession/limitation dispute over land between cotenants; no letting or lodging of a dwelling for pay.

Contract dispute over construction of an ice-manufacturing plant and damages for delay; entirely a commercial construction-contract case, no lodging/boarding house content despite selector match on 'lease' terminology.

Landlord's lien/waiver dispute over a leased store house used for a mercantile business (long-term commercial lease, assigned between merchants); not a dwelling or lodging arrangement, so outside the corpus's scope despite general landlord-tenant lien doctrine.
Dispute over municipal ad valorem tax levy limits for a city of over 10,000 inhabitants; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
Trespass-to-try-title action over a strip of land used as an alleyway, turning on limitations title and a defective married-woman's acknowledgment; no lodging/boarding content.
Title dispute turning on validity of an 1856 estate administration and a subsequent land lease/tenancy dispute over undeveloped acreage; not a lodging or boarding-house case.

Suit by a corporate landlord (Beaumont Temperance Hall Co.) against a tenant holding over on a multi-year monthly lease of a house and lot; an ordinary commercial landlord-tenant rent/possession dispute, not a household lodging or short-term letting arrangement.
Cotenants' conveyance of a railway right-of-way and subsequent partition of remaining acreage; a real-property/cotenancy case with no lodging or boarding house issue.
Cotenancy/partition and title dispute over land; no letting, lodging, or boarding-house content.
Title dispute over an interest in the 'Cosmopolitan Hotel' property; case turns on quitclaim deeds and limitations, not on the legal character of hotel/lodging-keeping.
Negligence case over a child's death; that the mother 'kept a boarding house' is background explaining household duties, not an adjudication of lodging/boarding law.
Cotenancy dispute over damages from a railway-caused grass fire on jointly owned pasture land; no letting/lodging content.
Agricultural cropping/tenancy dispute over ownership of a cotton crop and conversion by ginners; not residential room letting.
Cotenancy dispute over one cotenant's right to sell timber from jointly owned land; no letting/lodging content.
Judge-disqualification issue in a trespass-to-try-title suit; no letting/lodging content.
Adverse-possession dispute over a ranch house occupied intermittently for stock operations; not compensated occupancy by lodgers or boarders.
Dispute over the right to purchase state school land, turning on a settler's tenant/possession chain; not a lodging arrangement.
Landlord-tenant fixture dispute over a stairway installed in a leased commercial storehouse used as a saloon; no lodging content.

new.holding_summary: The court held that furniture used by a family in its own home for the family's comfort remains exempt 'household furniture' even where boarders are taken in under specific contracts for the family's support, so long as the house is not held open to the public as a business like a hotel or restaurant. Whether the appellee's furniture was so used, or was instead furniture kept for operating a commercial lodging house, was a fact question that should have gone to the jury, so the case was reversed and remanded.

quotes.text: said property at the time of its alleged seizure was not used by appellee’s family, but was used by him in keeping a lodging house, and therefore did not come within the exemption provided by statute.

Mrs. Byrne was a widow, who for the support of herself and child seems to have been compelled to take boarders, who occupied rooms in the house; but such boarders as she received were selected and fed and lodged under specific contracts, and at no time was the house open to the public.

It seems to us that personal property held only for purposes of business, such as that of hotel or restaurant keeping, ought not to be held ‘ household furniture ’ within the meaning of statutes giving exemptions, although that used by a family in the same building for the use and comfort of the family might be; for in the one case the property is held and used for purpose of business and profit, to secure which this particular' exemption is not given; while in the other the exemption is given to secure the necessities, comforts, and conveniences of the family in a home.

It seems to us that personal property held only for purposes of business, such as that of hotel or restaurant keeping, ought not to be held ‘ household furniture ’ within the meaning of statutes giving exemptions, although that used by a family in the same building for the use and comfort of the family might be; for in the one case the property is held and used for purpose of business and profit, to secure which this particular' exemption is not given; while in the other the exemption is given to secure the necessities, comforts, and conveniences of the family in a home.

new.notes: Merits of whether Woods's own use was family lodging vs. commercial lodging-house business were remanded to the jury; quotes state the governing legal standard, drawn partly from the court's approving citation of Muller v. Richardson (Mrs. Byrne).
Libel action over bad-debt collection letters; plaintiff's occupation as a boarding-house keeper is background only and is not adjudicated by the court.
Ten-year commercial real-estate lease breach and limitations dispute; not short-term room letting.

Land title/limitation dispute among cotenants; no lodging content.

Forcible entry and detainer over a family dwelling following a real-estate exchange; ordinary residential tenancy, not short-term room letting or boarding.

Ordinary full-house lease, not the room/lodging practice this corpus targets.

Cropper/landowner dispute over crops raised on shares and conversion damages; no bearing on lodging or letting of dwellings.
Municipal stock-impoundment ordinance under police power; concerns animals running at large, not lodging or boarding.
Purely a venue dispute over where rent for a leased hotel building could be sued for; the hotel is mentioned only incidentally, with no discussion of lodging practice or its legal character.
Fire insurance dispute over a policy's vacancy clause for a dwelling house; a brief tenancy is mentioned but the case is entirely about insurance law, not lodging.

Commercial landlord-tenant dispute over a tenant's right to remove buildings/fixtures from leased ground; not about lodging or boarding.
Trespass-to-try-title contest turning on adverse possession by tenants on farmland; tenants mentioned are agricultural occupants, not lodgers/boarders.
Construction of the landlord's-lien statute for a leased store-house against competing attachment creditors; a commercial lease dispute, not lodging.
General landlord-tenant estoppel and joinder-of-actions doctrine over possession and rent of real property; no lodging/boarding facts.
Tenant's right to dispute landlord's title after purchasing a superior title, involving a leased town lot; no lodging/boarding facts.

Local-option liquor license revocation case; no mention of lodging, boarding, or dwelling letting.
Agricultural land lease/trespass (tenant grazing rented field, turning stock loose); no dwelling/lodging letting.

Trespass-to-try-title evidentiary rule re: judgments against a subtenant; land title dispute, not lodging.
Commercial lot leased monthly to a holdover tenant; jurisdictional dispute over trespass to try title, not a dwelling/lodging arrangement.
Abstract landlord-tenant estoppel doctrine (tenant cannot deny landlord's title); no facts involving dwelling/room letting or lodging.
Forcible detainer/estoppel doctrine over leased premises generally; no lodging or boarding facts.
Tenants-in-common rents/profits accounting rule; not a landlord-lodger arrangement.
Duplicate reporter entry of Moore v. Crenshaw & Luckey; municipal animal-impounding ordinance, no lodging content.

Landlord's statutory lien on tenant's mules/crop supplies; agricultural tenancy dispute, no dwelling letting.

Municipal ordinance on cattle running at large and appeal-bond procedure; livestock impounding, not lodging houses.
Police-power discussion is about municipal impounding/sale of stray livestock, not licensing or regulation of lodging/boarding houses.
Municipal occupation-tax/police-power case re: railway ticket brokers/scalpers; no connection to lodging or boarding houses.

new.holding_summary: The County Court affirmed (as modified) convictions of a hospital partnership for renting more rooms/persons than the residential zoning ordinance permitted for lodging or boarding purposes in two dwellings adjoining the hospital, rejecting defenses that the employee-occupants formed a 'family' or that the use was 'accessory' to the hospital. The court struck the anticipatory daily-fine provision but let the underlying $100 fines stand.

quotes.text: Not more than two rooms may be rented for lodging or boarding purposes in any one dwelling, and to not more than a total of four persons, provided, however, that such persons do not have separate cooking facilities; nor shall they be permitted to do independent cooking on the premises.
The defendants, therefore, have failed to show that the occupancy of the buildings involved here was “ accessory use ”.
The judgments of conviction, as modified, are affirmed.

new.notes: Duration left unclear: opinion establishes employees resided in the houses in connection with hospital employment but gives no explicit length of stay.

new.holding_summary: The Supreme Court held that an owner-occupant sharing his house with three to seven other men who each contributed a monthly sum toward expenses was, despite the 'ingenious' cost-sharing arrangement, operating a boarding house rather than maintaining a 'single family dwelling.' It permanently enjoined him from using the premises as a boarding or rooming house under the town's residential zoning ordinance.

quotes.text: It seems to us that defendant’s actual status or service is similar to a hoarding house keeper, and that he has been such at all times notwithstanding the ingenious form of his economic arrangement.

the defendant his agents, employees, assigns and successors in interest be and they hereby are enjoined and restrained from keeping, maintaining, and operating and using the premises described in the complaint for a boarding house or rooming house or for similar uses
We have concluded that defendant’s position is untenable.

new.notes: Quote for characterization preserves OCR error 'hoarding' (for 'boarding') exactly as printed.

new.court: City Court of the City of New York, Trial Term, New York County
new.holding_summary: The City Court dismissed plaintiff's forcible-entry-and-detainer claim, holding that because defendants were innkeepers and plaintiff occupied a hotel room (without registering and without a lawful assignment from the prior guest), she was never in possession of real property and thus was not 'put out' within the meaning of the Real Property Law when defendants changed the lock. The court found the innkeepers' conduct lawful, though it declined to endorse it.

quotes.text: Defendants were innkeepers, and plaintiff occupied, a room in their hotel.
but they acted lawfully and are not answerable in damages to plaintiff.
Judgment may be entered in favor of defendants dismissing the complaint.

new.notes: Marked mixed: court found the innkeeper's room-management conduct lawful (favorable to commercial short-term letting practice) while expressly withholding approval of that conduct and denying the occupant any protection.

new.court: Supreme Court, Special Term, Westchester County
new.holding_summary: In an Article 78 proceeding, the Supreme Court ordered the Yonkers superintendent of buildings to issue a permit for a proposed thirty-two-room motel-type structure, holding that it met the zoning ordinance's definition of a 'hotel' and was therefore a permitted use in the district, even though the ordinance predated the modern 'motel' concept.

quotes.text: The instant application, if it does not meet the definition of an apartment, certainly meets the definition of a hotel.
The building for which a permit is here sought is clearly within the permitted uses of the ordinance.
Petition granted.

the word ‘private’ further restricts the buildings to be placed thereon by excluding all such as are used for residential purposes of a public character, like hotels and general public boarding or apartment-houses.

there is a well-defined difference between an apartment-house operated by the owner for profit through leasing different stories or suites of rooms and a dwelling intended and calculated to be for the sole and exclusive occupancy of one family, suitably constructed for that purpose.

we, therefore, declare and advise, as a declaratory judgment or decree, that, in our opinion, the restriction in petitioner’s deed prohibits use of any structure hereafter erected on his premises as an apartment-house.

Contractor/materialman lien priority dispute over buildings erected on land not owned by the builder; no letting/lodging issue.
Party-wall demolition/damages dispute between neighbors; rent reduction mentioned only as one item of consequential damages, not a letting/lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: The court affirmed judgment for the defendant lessee, holding that a lessor cannot recover rent under a lease he knew at signing was for an unlawful purpose; here the lessor knew the lessee, an unmarried woman taking a house far larger than she needed for herself, intended to run it as a lodging/assignation house outside the city's restricted district fixed by ordinance, and the lease was therefore unenforceable.

quotes.text: she could only intend the property as a lodging house

Section 1 of Ordinance No. 6701 N. C. S. adopted August ^¡2d, 1910 prescribes the limits of the restricted district, and ^Section 2 makes it unlawful for any person to rent any house to ^lewd woman outside of those limits.

maintain the doctrine that no action arises from a contract of lease when the lessor was aware at the time it was made that the leased premises were to be used for a purpose forbidden by law and whan the premises were so used subsequently.

new.notes: Marginal adverse authority: a municipal ordinance restricted where a house let out for lodging/assignation use could operate, and the lease was voided on that basis; the underlying use was prostitution rather than ordinary boarding, so weight accordingly.
Commercial hotel-property sublease dispute over renewal rights between lessor, lessee, and subtenant beer distributors; no lodging/boarding-house letting or regulation issue.
Ordinary landlord repair-liability suit by a tenant's wife injured by falling plaster; standard residential tenancy, not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Ordinary landlord negligence suit by a lessee's wife injured by falling window glass; standard residential tenancy, not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Petitory action/succession title dispute over land; a tenant's failure to name his lessor is a procedural side issue, no lodging/boarding content.
Ordinary landlord repair-liability suit by a lessee's guest injured by a defective step; standard residential tenancy, not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Injunction/contempt proceeding over enforcement of a restaurant/musical-performance ordinance against the police inspector; no lodging or boarding-house content.

Sustains a 'disorderly house' statute against a dance-hall/theater operator for permitting lewd dancing; the statutory definition covers public entertainment venues and prostitution but does not mention or implicate boarding/lodging houses.
Commercial garage sublease/eviction dispute over which assignee is the proper defendant; no lodging/boarding content.
Quasi-partnership dispute between a jeweler and optician sharing a leased commercial store building; no residential letting or lodging issue.
Constitutional dispute over the validity of a municipal public-utilities board's appointment method; unrelated to lodging/boarding.
Lease-vs-license dispute over Coney Island candy-stand concession stalls; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding-house issue.

new.holding_summary: The court held that 'The Lucerne,' an apartment building whose suites were rented under annual leases without soliciting transient tenants, was not a 'hotel' within the meaning of the 1895 civil-rights statute. Because it was an ordinary letting of apartments rather than innkeeping, the proprietor could lawfully exercise the ordinary landlord's right to select tenants and refuse to lease to the plaintiff.

quotes.text: These apartments are rented upon annual leases and transient tenants are not solicited.

Tested by this definition “ The Lucerne ” is certainly not an hotel, and when the defendant refused to lease apartments to the plaintiff it exercised only the right which every landlord .undoubtedly has to ’make his own selection of tenants.

A house where all who conduct themselves properly, and who are able and ready to pay for their entertainment, are received, if there is accommodation for them, and who, without any stipulated engagement as to the duration of their stay, or as to the rate of compensation, are, while there, supplied at a reasonable charge with their meals, their 'lodging, and such services and attention as are necessarily incident to the use of the house as a temporary home.

new.notes: Turns on the duration-of-stay test distinguishing hotel/innkeeping from ordinary annual apartment letting; letting treated as ordinary incident of ownership giving proprietor tenant-selection discretion.
Ordinary apartment-house landlord/tenant dispute over house rules and constructive eviction from noise; no lodging/short-let issue.
Innkeeper liability for a stolen horse left in the stable; concerns guest/inn status for property bailment, not compensated human occupancy of a dwelling.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Term, First Department
new.notes: Dispute over who was landlord (trustee vs. association) under a printing-plant lease; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Tort case on landlord's duty to repair and liability for a tenant's guest injured by a falling ceiling; does not bear on legality/character of letting.
Private alley easement/right-of-way dispute among adjoining lot owners with old private-stable restrictions; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting.
Trade-name/unfair-competition suit between an apartment house and a hotel both named 'Apthorp'; describes but does not adjudicate the legal character of the letting arrangements.
Tenant-at-will use-and-occupation claim over former woolen-mill factory buildings; no dwelling/lodging issue.

Tenement House Law fire-escape/fire-safety case turning on whether a building was 'intended, arranged or designed' for three-family occupancy; concerns family occupancy classification, not compensated lodging or boarding-house regulation.
Fire-insurance 'vacant and unoccupied' forfeiture clause dispute; owner's husband slept in the house between tenancies, no compensated occupancy at issue.

new.holding_summary: The Appellate Term reversed a judgment for a tenant who had leased an apartment-hotel suite for a year and stopped paying rent after learning the hotel also let rooms to transient guests. The court held that letting some rooms to transients did not breach any covenant of quiet enjoyment absent an express restriction in the written lease confining the building to non-transient apartment use.

quotes.text: There is not, however, the slightest proof in the case that the renting of rooms to transients in any degree interfered with defendant's beneficial enjoyment of the rooms rented to him.

but it seems to me, if he intended to have his tenancy conditional upon such an exclusive occupancy of the building, he should not have executed the lease unless it contained a clause safeguarding his rights in that respect, and clearly expressing the agreement in that behalf between the parties.

new.notes: Affirms hotel operator's right to let rooms to transient guests alongside annual-lease tenants absent an express restrictive covenant.
Holdover-tenant/lease-termination dispute over a factory building; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Same trade-name dispute as case_id 2808585 (Astor 'Apthorp' apartment house vs. hotel), reported in a different reporter; unfair-competition holding, not a letting-legality holding.
Breach of covenant for quiet enjoyment via wrongful ejectment suits over a leased printing office; commercial lease, not dwelling/lodging.

School-tuition residency/domicile case; family rented ordinary apartment rooms as tenants for a school year. Retrieved on an in-passing citation to a boarding-house-keeper case (Stacom v. Moon), but the holding itself does not adjudicate letting/lodging legality.
Splitting-a-cause-of-action rule for rent claims arising from a municipal tenancy-from-year-to-year; procedural rent litigation, not lodging/short-let doctrine.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Dispute over a farmhouse lease during a municipal water-supply condemnation proceeding; concerns landlord's title, tenant estoppel, and rent obligations, with no bearing on short-term room letting or boarding/lodging.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Innkeeper's liability for a horse left overnight in the inn's stable; concerns the guest/host relationship for stabling animals, not the letting of rooms or dwellings to human occupants.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Allocates penalty liability between owner and 21-year lessee under the Tenement House Law for failing to supply garbage/ash receptacles; addresses municipal sanitary-code liability allocation, not the practice or character of compensated room/dwelling letting.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Personal-injury demurrer case about a landlord's tort liability, if any, to a tenant's 'lodger, visitor, or member of the tenant's family' injured by a falling ceiling covered under a repair covenant; 'lodger' is used only as a status label for a tenant's household member, not to address compensated room-letting arrangements.

Innkeeper-guest dispute over a disputed café bill and the admissibility of reputation evidence in a suit for wrongful exclusion from the dining room; concerns innkeeper's right to refuse service for nonpayment and evidentiary rules, not the character or regulation of room/dwelling letting.
Mandamus proceeding over denial of a garage permit near a school under a fire-prevention ordinance; a police-power case about gasoline storage, unrelated to lodging/boarding house letting.
Condemnation-award dispute over riparian boundary lines and title to land under a creek; no bearing on room/dwelling letting.
Public nuisance action over a railroad trestle bridge and fill obstructing a navigable creek; concerns navigable-waters law, not lodging or dwelling letting.
Dispute over whether a mercantile tenant renewed a commercial store lease or held over without landlord consent; ordinary commercial landlord-tenant dispute with no lodging/boarding dimension.

Construes the Tenement House Law penalty for a tenement 'used ... for the purpose of prostitution,' holding a single undiscovered act of vice by occupants is insufficient absent some continuity of use; concerns illegal use of tenement rooms, not the character or regulation of lawful compensated room-letting/lodging.

Murder appeal turning on admissibility of the defendant's confessions before a coroner and district attorney; that the defendant 'kept a boarding house' and the victim was her boarder is a passing background fact, not a holding about boarding-house letting.
Franchise-tax dispute over whether a railroad holding company that leased its railroad to another corporation was 'doing business' in New York; corporate tax law, no bearing on room/dwelling letting.

Civil Rights Act case holding a theatre may exclude a dramatic critic for reasons other than race, creed, or color; the statutory definition of 'place of public accommodation' it construes lists inns/hotels for transient or health/rest guests, but the dispute itself concerns theatre admission, not room/dwelling letting.

Damages action over a railroad's construction and operation of a rail line across lots restricted by covenant to private-dwelling use only; concerns eminent domain/restrictive-covenant compensation for railroad construction, not compensated room or dwelling letting.

Case concerns a lease renewal option, partnership dissolution among joint lessees of a skating rink, and admissibility of evidence of tenant misconduct in a trespass/eviction suit against an unincorporated market association; no bearing on lodging or boarding.
Dispute over whether a subtenant corporation (House of Refuge) verbally agreed to a new year-to-year sublease versus its written sixty-days-notice lease; no lodging/boarding issue.
Landlord's distraint on a stranger's soda-fountain apparatus for tenant's rent, and whether the equipment lease was a bailment or conditional sale; unrelated to lodging/boarding.

Suit by hotel landlords against a tenant's sureties after tenant abandoned the premises for failure to repair heating; 'boarders would not stay and transient guests would not patronize the hotel' is cited only as evidence of the hotel's lost business, not as a holding on the legal character of lodging/boarding.

Physician-office tenants sued landlord for breach of implied covenant of quiet enjoyment after she leased the rest of the building to a hotel/bar operator; addresses scope of the quiet-enjoyment covenant, not the legality or regulation of letting rooms or boarding.
Equity suit over coal mining waste under an 1821 agricultural lease and use of mine passageways; no lodging/boarding issue.

Will-construction dispute over whether a life-estate devise of 'the premises occupied by me' to testator's housekeeper included a portion of the building rented to a bank as tenant; concerns testamentary construction of 'occupied,' not letting/boarding law.

Statutory proceeding to frame an ejectment issue over possession of a two-acre lot with several dwellings; tenants' rent payments are discussed only as evidence of adverse possession, not as a lodging/boarding holding.
Dispute over whether a tenant's rent payment to the landlord's wife (co-owner by entireties) satisfied the lease obligation; concerns tenancy-by-entireties property law, not lodging/boarding.

Prohibition-era liquor confiscation/search-warrant case construing 'private dwelling' under the Snyder Act; 'boarding house' appears only as one entry in a list of business uses (store, shop, saloon, restaurant, hotel, boarding house, warehouse, public garage) that strip a dwelling of search protection — dicta about liquor search law, not a holding on lodging/boarding regulation.
Commercial lease abandonment/surrender and reletting-liability dispute between a landlord and a business tenant's receivers; unrelated to lodging/boarding.

new.court: Lancaster County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Suit between an estranged husband and wife over rent the husband collected from a tenant on entireties property, and his right to apply it to repairs/mortgage interest; not about lodging/boarding.
Equity-jurisdiction/pleading dispute over a title-cloud bill properly certified to the law side as an ejectment action; no lodging/boarding issue.
Injunction dispute between adjoining landowners over a claimed parol-grant/prescriptive right of way (alley); unrelated to lodging.
Easement dispute over shared privy-vault sections serving four adjoining dwelling lots, resolved on implied-grant/implied-reservation doctrine; unrelated to lodging/boarding.
Criminal liquor-license case over whether an eating-house license limited to vinous/malt/brewed liquors barred sale of spirituous liquor (whiskey); unrelated to lodging/boarding regulation.
Municipal police-power case invalidating a market ordinance forbidding resale of goods bought at a public market; concerns market/commerce regulation, not lodging or boarding house licensing.
Corporate stock-reorganization breach-of-contract dispute; 'rent houses' is one incidental clause in a business letter about tenant housing management, unrelated to lodging/boarding doctrine.

quotes.text: Since the houses were erected they have been rented whenever tenants could be obtained.
We rented them by the month, sometimes by the week, just as it happened.
I had no other means for providing for my family, and put up the houses on B and A for renting, and used this money for supplying my family.

new.notes: Primarily a homestead-exemption case; letting the extra houses is treated as an ordinary, unremarkable income-producing use of the property (no suggestion it was unlawful), though it defeated the homestead claim. Only tangentially bears on the corpus's core letting doctrine.
Homestead-exemption case about a father renting out farm land/crops on behalf of his minor children; concerns agricultural land rental, not letting of rooms or dwellings to lodgers/boarders.

new.holding_summary: The court held that two rent houses built and let by a brother and sister on part of their family homestead did not work an abandonment of the homestead, because the renting was temporary and not intended to permanently segregate the lot, the family retained partial use of the ground, and tenants performed household services (washing) in exchange for occupancy.

quotes.text: Where there is only a temporary renting of a part of the homestead and no segregation made or intended, it does not constitute a divestiture of the homestead character as to such portion.
he had never abandoned the idea of -using any part of the west lot upon which the rent houses were situated as a home

these houses were occupied by families who did his sister’s washing and other services for the family, presumably, in payment for their use, which tends to show a home or family use of the houses, as contradistinguished from the independent use of them by renters.

new.notes: Homestead-abandonment case; treats temporary letting of extra houses on the family lot as ordinary, non-disqualifying use. Tangential to the core letting doctrine but supports the 'ordinary incident of ownership' framing.

General premises-liability licensee/invitee doctrine involving a tramroad and tie inspection; the 'license' discussion is generic negligence law, unconnected to letting rooms/dwellings or lodging-house regulation.
Covenant-against-incumbrances dispute concerning a farm tenant's unexpired lease at the time of a land sale; not about letting rooms/dwellings or boarding/lodging.

Fraud-based lease-cancellation suit over a landlord's ordinary rental houses managed by an agent; whole-house month-to-month tenancies, not lodging/boarding or room-letting within an occupied dwelling.
Ordinary month-to-month residential house lease and rent dispute between owner and tenant; no lodging, boarding, or room-letting element.
Farm-lease and option-to-renew/tenancy-at-will dispute over a large tract; unrelated to letting of dwelling rooms or lodging/boarding.
Fire-insurance dispute over whether a rented dwelling was 'vacant or unoccupied' for policy purposes; ordinary tenant occupancy of a house, not lodging/boarding-house doctrine.

new.holding_summary: The court held that a building permit issued and relied on before a later fire-prevention ordinance took effect vested the permittee's right to complete construction, and denied a mandatory injunction to remove the completed building because the plaintiff's nearby family hotel was not shown to face any material fire hazard from it.

quotes.text: there was located on plaintiff’s lots an 18-room, two-story frame building, owned by plaintiff, and operated by her as a family hotel.
there was located on plaintiff’s lots an 18-room, two-story frame building, owned by plaintiff, and operated by her as a family hotel.

If the building of plaintiff was found not to be subject to any material fire hazard by reason of the construction of the said building, she is shown to be without injury, and this finding of the court concludes her on the issue of damages

new.notes: The plaintiff's family hotel is background fact (she is the injured party seeking an injunction against a neighbor's building), not the object of the legal dispute; the hotel's own operation is treated as an ordinary, legitimate business entitled to protection. Tangential relevance.
Commercial lease-assignment dispute over subletting a building for use as a garage; unrelated to residential lodging or room-letting doctrine.

new.holding_summary: The court held that the statutory liability cap for hotel/boarding house keepers (Tex. Rev. Civ. Stat. art. 4592) applies only where every lock or bolt placed on a guest's door is suitable; because the hotel's supplemental night-latch bolt was defective and a guest's property was stolen through it, the $50 statutory limitation did not apply and the hotel was liable for the full loss.

quotes.text: Any hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house keeper, who constantly has in his hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house a metal safe or vault in good order and fit for the custody of money, jewelry, articles of gold or silver manufacture, precious stones, personal ornaments, or documents of any kind, and who keeps on the doors of the sleeping rooms used by guests suitable locks or bolts and proper fastenings on the transom and window of said room, shall not be liable for the loss or injury suffered by any guest on account of the loss of said valuables in excess of the sum of Fifty Dollars

Any hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house keeper, who constantly has in his hotel, apartment hotel or boarding house a metal safe or vault in good order and fit for the custody of money, jewelry, articles of gold or silver manufacture, precious stones, personal ornaments, or documents of any kind, and who keeps on the doors of the sleeping rooms used by guests suitable locks or bolts and proper fastenings on the transom and window of said room, shall not be liable for the loss or injury suffered by any guest on account of the loss of said valuables in excess of the sum of Fifty Dollars
We do not believe that a hotel keeper, under the law, can place more than one lock or bolt, or both a lock and a bolt, on the door of his sleeping room doors, one of which may be unsuitable or unsafe

new.notes: Applies a statute regulating hotel/apartment-hotel/boarding-house keepers' liability for guests' property; the regulation is enforced strictly against the operator, so it is coded adverse (regulation of the lodging business sustained and applied against the keeper).
Cotenancy/adverse-possession land-partition dispute; the 'rents and revenues' referenced are from farm land collected by a family member, not from letting rooms or dwellings.

new.holding_summary: The court held that a landlord's breach of a covenant to repair a leaking roof did not excuse the tenant's rent obligation for months he continued to use and occupy the building as a grocery store and rooming house, absent proof the leaks rendered the building unfit for use or any counterclaim for offsetting damages.

quotes.text: J. A. Woolly occupied and used the building as a grocery store on the first floor, and as a rooming house on the second floor.
J. A. Woolly occupied and used the building as a grocery store on the first floor, and as a rooming house on the second floor.
appellee was liable for the rent for the three months' admitted use and occupancy of the building.

new.notes: The tenant's operation of a rooming house on the leased premises' second floor is undisputed background fact; the court's actual holding concerns the repair covenant and rent liability, not the legality of the rooming house use itself.

new.holding_summary: The court affirmed a temporary mandatory injunction restoring possession of a residence to its owners, finding that the occupants (who used the premises as a boarding and rooming house) held over after their month-to-month tenancy expired without any enforceable right to an extension, and were therefore naked trespassers wrongfully in possession.

quotes.text: that said premises are being used for a boarding and rooming house, to the detriment and injury of the plaintiffs
that said premises are being used for a boarding and rooming house, to the detriment and injury of the plaintiffs
said defendants are wrongfully in possession of said premises, and without any legal right or claim thereto, and are naked trespassers wrongfully in possession of said premises

new.notes: Plaintiffs' petition frames the defendants' use of the residence as a boarding and rooming house as a source of injury/detriment to the owners, and the court's judgment treats the occupants as unlawful trespassers rather than protected tenants; coded adverse.

Same underlying dispute as case_id 619026 (Jef Chaison Townsite Co. v. Beaumont Sawmill Co.), reported in a different reporter; 'rent houses' is again only an incidental phrase in a quoted business letter, unrelated to lodging/boarding doctrine.

new.holding_summary: The court held that a house and lot bought and operated by an unmarried daughter as a boarding/rooming house, separately titled, taxed, insured, and mortgaged in her name alone, never became part of her father's homestead simply because the family moved into it after their original home burned, since no member of the household was shown to be dependent on any single member as head of a family.

quotes.text: This house was at 1003 Washington street, and was used as a boarding house.
This house was at 1003 Washington street, and was used as a boarding house.

was never any part of the homestead at No. 927 Washington Street, and was never owned by the parents of the three women named in this suit, and consequently up to the time that the home at 927 was burned had not been impressed with the homestead character.

new.notes: A homestead/mechanic's-lien case in which the daughter's independent operation of a boarding/rooming house (renting rooms, paying taxes, mortgaging in her own name) is what keeps the property outside the homestead exemption; the rooming house business itself is treated as an ordinary, lawful commercial enterprise.
Succession partition-in-kind case (580-acre tract); 'suitable for a dwelling for her' refers to the widow needing a house, not compensated lodging/boarding. No lodging or letting issue at all.
Venue dispute over a dog-bite tort action; 'trespass' language matched selectors but has nothing to do with lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: A householder who registered part of her apartment as two sleeping rooms with kitchen privileges under OPA rent regulations, rather than as a single apartment, did not thereby commit an unlawful 'evasion' of the lower apartment rent ceiling; she was entitled to rent the space either way, and the higher ceiling for the sleeping-room registration governed.

quotes.text: I want to rent out individual rooms in my apartment as sleeping rooms only. Can I do this? A. Generally, if your apartment is vacant, you may rent out rooms for sleeping purposes only. However, you must register under the Hotel and Roominghouse Regulation and you are subject to its provisions if you rent to more than two paying tenants.

In renting her quarters to these plaintiffs defendant performed no wrongful, fraudulent or illegal act. Her actions amounted only to the legally permitted avoidance of an alternate and a lower rental' ceiling.
the three plaintiffs took possession of the accommodations at a rental of $75 per month, to the payment of which they had agreed two days previously.

new.notes: Householder rented two rooms of her own apartment (with shared kitchen privileges) as sleeping accommodations under OPA rent control; court upheld her right to structure the letting this way as an ordinary, lawful exercise of ownership, not an evasion of rent regulation.

Zoning non-conforming-use case about renting space for house trailers on a residential lot; occupants live in their own trailers, not the landowner's dwelling/rooms. 'Rent house' appears only as a rejected analogy in argument, not as an adjudicated holding about letting rooms/dwellings.

Mandamus suit over a building-permit refusal to relocate a residence within a zoning district; the phrase 'rent house' appears only as a label handwritten on the permit application describing intended future use. Case turns entirely on zoning procedure/police power for permits, not on any adjudicated lodging or letting arrangement.
Premises-liability case involving a trespasser/licensee injured in a lumber yard. 'License' terminology matched selectors but concerns tort licensee doctrine, not lodging or dwelling letting.

A rezoning petition alleges the neighborhood is already full of apartments, rooming-houses, boarding-houses, and rent houses, but the court never reaches that factual characterization — the suit is dismissed on exception of no cause of action on separation-of-powers grounds (courts cannot control legislative zoning amendment procedure). No judicial holding on the lodging/letting practice itself.

Petitory action against multiple land occupants/trespassers turning on misjoinder of parties defendant; some defendants had paid 'rent' but the case is entirely about joinder/title procedure, not lodging or dwelling letting.
Bond-for-deed/title dispute over a vacant lot used for gardening and livestock; 'use and occupancy' rent claim relates to land, not a dwelling or rooms let for lodging.
Lessor's lien dispute over a victrola removed from a commercially leased storefront; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Servitude-by-acquiescence dispute over a drainage canal on plaintiff's land; discussion of 'rent' concerns whether a public utility must pay rent for land use, unrelated to dwelling lodging.
Personal-injury case about a pedestrian's licensee status on a railroad bridge; 'license' matched selectors but has no connection to lodging or dwelling letting.

quotes.text: This is a suit by a landlord against a tenant to recover, the sum of $225 representing rent alleged to be due for the months of May, June, and July, 1932, at the rate of $75 per month, under an oral month to month lease, and for recognition and maintenance of the lessor's lien and privilege on the furniture and effects in the premises.
the record shows that the plaintiff stated that the building was used as a rooming house, whereas the defendant said that she had used the premises for immoral purposes.

new.notes: Whole building was leased by plaintiff to defendant, who apparently operated it as a rooming house; court enforced the ordinary month-to-month lease/rent claim without adjudicating the rooming-house or immoral-use characterization (excluded for failure to specially plead). Marked mixed given the unresolved assignation-house allegation alongside routine lease enforcement.

Eviction action under the Share Croppers Act turning on a void interracial marriage and a homestead declaration; no lodging/letting issue despite selector match on 'renting her quarters'-style embedding.
Separation from bed and board / custody / alimony case; no lodging or dwelling-letting content.
Police-power zoning/permit dispute over operation of an oil filling station and garage; ordinance-publication procedure case, unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.
Mandamus suit to compel a city council to act on a proposed ordinance regulating firemen's working hours; wholly unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.

Dispute over a rent receiver's authority to bring summary nonpayment proceedings after a foreclosure receivership was vacated; ordinary commercial lease dispute with no bearing on short-term letting or lodging.

Restrictive-covenant construction case over whether 'first class private residences' bars apartment houses/hotels; rooming/lodging houses are mentioned only in passing as evidence of neighborhood change, never adjudicated.

new.holding_summary: The court held that the defendant's building was an apartment hotel supplying customary hotel services within the meaning of Lien Law section 181, so the landlord held both a statutory and a contractual lien on the tenant's furniture, and dismissed the former tenants' replevin action to recover it.

quotes.text: An apartment hotel within the meaning of this section includes a hotel wherein apartments are rented for fixed periods of time, either furnished or unfurnished, to the occupants of which the keeper of such hotel supplies food, if required.

An apartment hotel within the meaning of this section includes a hotel wherein apartments are rented for fixed periods of time, either furnished or unfurnished, to the occupants of which the keeper of such hotel supplies food, if required.

It, therefore, appears clearly to me that the defendant in these two cases has a hen on ah the property of the plaintiffs contained in their apartment, both under the provisions of the Lien Law and also by virtue of the expressed stipulation in the lease itself. The complaint will, therefore, be dismissed on the merits, without prejudice to another action by the plaintiffs, after they shah have paid or tendered the amount due to the defendant.

new.notes: Bears on legal character of compensated occupancy: whether an unfurnished suite in a building offering extensive hotel services counts as an 'apartment hotel' (innkeeping) for landlord's-lien purposes, not on the legitimacy of householder letting itself.
Summary proceeding over a stockholder's rent-free occupancy of an apartment in lieu of corporate dividends; ordinary tenancy-at-will/foreclosure dispute, not lodging or short-term letting.

Restrictive-covenant dispute over a cocktail lounge/bar in a 'family hotel'; addresses covenant construction and competitive-use limits, not the legality or regulation of short-term room letting generally.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: The court held that the tenant's subletting of five apartments for single-room occupancy did not violate the Multiple Dwelling Law where the landlord had long acquiesced in the arrangement, and that rent regulation's protection against removal extended to the subtenants because subletting the accommodations was within the parties' contemplation from the outset.

quotes.text: In this proceeding for dispossession of tenant and undertenants on the ground that the demised premises in a class A fireproof multiple dwelling are being used illegally for single-room occupancy and do not conform with section 248 of the Multiple Dwelling Law, no notice of violation of that section was served by the department of housing and buildings.

There is no occupancy for “ an immoral or illegal purpose ” here. Further it is fair to assume that when these five or more •apartments were let to the tenant Nelson a subleasing of the accommodations or units was within the contemplation of the parties, the subtenants or other occupants being thus brought within the protection of the regulation by the amendment of paragraph (1) of subdivision (c) of section 6.
The final order should be reversed, with $30 costs, and final order directed for tenant and undertenants, with costs.

new.notes: Single-room-occupancy subletting protected against removal; landlord's long acquiescence defeated the illegality claim.

new.court: New York Court of Special Sessions
new.holding_summary: The court found the arrangement between a practical nurse occupying part of her own two-family house and an invalid boarder's family was primarily a contract for nursing services with incidental use of rooms, not a landlord-tenant relationship subject to rent regulation, and reversed the appellant's convictions for rent overcharge, unlawful removal, and failure to register.

quotes.text: In our view, the agreement was an entire contract for services and accommodations and it could not be said beyond a reasonable doubt on the evidence adduced that, the agreement provided an apportionment as between rent and services. It is plainly evident that the primary purpose , of the arrangement was to secure nursing services and personal attention for complainant’s mother.
Considered as a contract for personal services, appellant could terminate it at will.
Accordingly, the three judgments are reversed and the complaints dismissed.

new.notes: Householder taking in a paying occupant along with personal-care services held outside rent-regulation's landlord-tenant framework entirely.

new.holding_summary: The court annulled the city rent commission's 30% rent increase for permanent hotel guests granted under a local law regulating hotel, apartment hotel, rooming house, and lodging house rents, holding the commission's 'hardship formula' and denial of a hearing to tenants were arbitrary and unlawful.

quotes.text: It is hereby declared that a serious emergency exists in the city of New York by reason of the shortage of housing accommodations, hotel, apartment hotel, rooming house and lodging house accommodations, by reason of which the safety and health of the inhabitants are seriously menaced.
The action of the commission was arbitrary and unlawful, and not in consonance with the purpose of the local law.

Accordingly, the application of the petitioner is granted, the determination of the commission is annulled and the matter remitted to the commission to proceed on the owner’s application in accordance with this opinion.

new.notes: Local law imposing rent stabilization on hotel/rooming/lodging house accommodations as a police-power emergency measure; this particular commission order was annulled on due-process grounds, but the underlying regulatory scheme is treated as legitimate.

new.holding_summary: The court denied the landlord's motion for a declaratory judgment terminating the tenant's lease of a furnished-room house and requiring surrender of the rooms occupied by subtenants, holding that federal rent regulation barred removal of the tenant (and derivatively the subtenants) absent a certificate from the local rent commission, since the premises were not entirely sublet.

quotes.text: By the terms of the lease the premises were to be occupied for dwelling purposes, or as a quiet, orderly, respectable furnished-room house.

new.holding_summary: Defendant, having represented to plaintiff during purchase negotiations that his remaining Fifth Avenue houses were restricted to and would always be first-class private residences, was equitably estopped from enlarging the adjoining house (over the shared party-wall) not as a private residence but for business purposes as part of a family hotel; the court restrained that use as an unauthorized encroachment on plaintiff's easement rights, though it noted defendant could still build on the party-wall to enlarge a private residence.

quotes.text: it is the use of the existing easement for purposes antagonistical to the expressed design of the defendant in building the houses, made patent by his statements and representations, which is complained of, and by which the house adjoining the plaintiff’s, to the prejudice of her property, as shown by the evidence, was enlarged, not as a private residence, but for business purposes, namely, as part of a family hotel.

Our judgment is, therefore, it appearing that plaintiff did not assent to the use of the party-wall between her and the adjoining premises for the erection of the additional stories which were made for business purposes, her right to protection from such a use by the defendant exists, and in equity and good conscience should be enforced

We do not wish to be understood, however, as declaring it to be our judgment that the defendant would have no right to build upon the party-wall," if the object were to enlarge his house as a private residence.
