Poor-law settlement dispute turning on whether a pauper family's year-long house tenancy (with rent paid) sufficed for legal settlement. Ordinary long-term family dwelling tenancy, not short-term letting/lodging; no boarding-house or lodger characterization issue.
Constructive-eviction dispute (water damage from landlord-built stairway) over rooms leased at monthly rent in a commercial building; no lodging/boarding facts.
Timber-cutting trespass/ejectment dispute; wholly unrelated to lodging.
Landlord's distraint of goods held by sheriff under a replevin writ (custodia legis doctrine); tenant leased apartments for a photography business. No issue of lodging/boarding characterization.
Ordinary dwelling-house lease made by an agent; replevin over distrained goods and dispute over whether rent paid to trustees after principal's death discharges the tenant. No lodging/boarding facts.
Farm lease; married woman's note given to release distrained property from a landlord's warrant. No dwelling/lodging issue.
Ordinary dwelling-house lease; replevin dispute over a sewing machine's exemption from distress for rent, and third-party goods on leased premises. No lodging/boarding facts.
Trespass by landlord for unroofing a leased storeroom used for cigar manufacturing, damaging tenant's goods. Commercial storeroom, not dwelling/lodging.

new.holding_summary: Boundary/ejectment dispute over a strip of land between a factory lot and adjoining dwelling lots, decided on the rule that monuments on the ground control courses and distances in a sheriff's deed.
new.notes: Retrieved only because 'Lodge' is a party surname; case concerns land-survey boundary law, not letting of rooms or lodgers.

new.cite: Cumberland Valley Railroad v. McLanahan, 59 Pa. 23
new.holding_summary: Ejectment by a tenant in common against a railroad company that built a warehouse beyond its chartered right of way on land held partly under a license from a co-tenant.
new.notes: Concerns railroad corporate powers and a license to occupy land for a warehouse, not household letting of dwelling rooms; retrieval matched generic ejectment/tenant language.

new.holding_summary: Ejectment involving competing paper titles, adverse possession, and the doctrine that a trustee holding legal title may sue all but the equitable owner.
new.notes: City-lot boundary and title dispute; no occupancy-for-pay or lodging issue present.

new.holding_summary: Holds that equity cannot enjoin a landlord's statutory Landlord and Tenant Act proceeding to recover possession, even though the underlying dispute involved a bank's lease of two rooms in a hotel building for banking purposes.
new.notes: Underlying facts involve a commercial lease of hotel rooms to a bank, but the opinion addresses only equity jurisdiction versus the statutory landlord-tenant remedy; no discussion of letting/lodging character or duration.

new.holding_summary: Dispute over a coal-mining lease's grant of use of tenements/railroad fixtures for extracting coal, holding that use for removing other coal was unauthorized and that assumpsit (rather than case) was the wrong form of action.
new.notes: 'Tenements' here means mining structures/cabins incident to a coal lease, not dwelling rooms let to lodgers.

new.holding_summary: In a suit on a marital separation agreement, holds that evidence of a parol side-agreement letting the wife occupy the husband's house rent-free until a date certain, and her failure to vacate, was admissible as a set-off.
new.notes: Wife's continued occupancy of husband's house after separation is a domestic-relations/support matter, not compensated letting of rooms to a lodger or boarder.

new.holding_summary: Holds a husband not liable, merely by virtue of his duty to support his wife, for rent on a house his wife had leased before their marriage and continued to occupy after it, while he himself resided elsewhere at a boarding-house.
new.notes: Husband's residence at 'his boarding-house' is a passing background fact; the holding concerns spousal liability for a pre-marital lease debt, not the legal character of lodging/boarding arrangements.

new.cite: Lanigan ex rel. Stichter v. Kille, 97 Pa. 120
new.holding_summary: Sets the measure of damages for a lessee evicted by paramount title from an ore-mining lease as the consideration paid, denying recovery for the value of mining improvements erected under covenant.
new.notes: Commercial mining lease and covenant-for-title damages case; unrelated to household lodging or boarding.

new.holding_summary: Holds that a landlord may appeal from a justice of the peace's decision allowing a tenant's set-off against rent under the Act of 1810, even though the tenant himself has no right of appeal.
new.notes: Ordinary dwelling-house tenancy rent/set-off appeal procedure; no lodging-house licensing or short-term letting issue.

new.holding_summary: In a summary proceeding for possession for non-payment of rent, holds the tenant may defend by showing the landlord's title has since been divested by a sheriff's sale under a judgment that encumbered it before the lease began.
new.notes: Ordinary rent-recovery/title-divestment dispute; not about lodging houses or short-term room letting.

new.cite: Reed v. Fidelity Insurance Trust & Safe Deposit Co., 113 Pa. 574
new.holding_summary: Holds that in partition among tenants in common, a mortgage lien on one co-tenant's undivided interest shifts from the land to the owelty payable to that co-tenant.
new.notes: Partition/lien-priority dispute among trust beneficiaries and tenants in common; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: Holds a railroad company could remove machinery and fixtures from a shop built on land granted subject to a reverter clause, up until actual abandonment of the site.
new.notes: Railroad land-grant reverter and fixture-removal dispute; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.

new.holding_summary: In distributing sheriff's-sale proceeds, holds that goods of a sub-tenant of a storeroom remain liable for the principal landlord's unpaid rent even though the sub-tenant had paid his own rent in full to the immediate lessee.
new.notes: Commercial storeroom sub-letting and distress-for-rent priority dispute; not household lodging.

new.holding_summary: Replevin case holding that an avowry for distress of rent in arrear need not state the exact amount due, and a landlord may recover less than the sum avowed.
new.notes: Lease of a store and barn; pure pleading/distress-for-rent technicality, unrelated to lodging.

new.holding_summary: Holds that an owner may not remove his half of a long-standing division fence built jointly with an adjoining landowner without consent, as the fence has become part of the realty.
new.notes: Boundary-fence dispute between adjoining owners; unrelated to lodging or letting.

new.holding_summary: Trespass action over a sawmill operator's refusal to divide manufactured lumber with the landowner under a wood-cutting agreement; holds an agent with no title until division cannot lawfully retain and remove the whole.
new.notes: Sawmill/timber-division contract dispute; unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.

new.holding_summary: Adopts the 'American doctrine' that no easement of light and air over an adjoining lot is implied from conveyance of a house with windows overlooking it, absent real necessity.
new.notes: Light-and-air easement dispute between adjoining lot owners; unrelated to lodging.

new.holding_summary: Holds an outgoing farm tenant may sell his right to the way-going crop, and the purchaser's claim survives a later settlement between landlord and tenant cancelling the lease.
new.notes: Agricultural farm-lease way-going-crop dispute; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
Dispute over obstruction of a right-of-way alley and equitable injunction; no letting, lodging, or boarding-house issue.
Judgment-lien revival and scire facias against terre-tenants; no bearing on letting of rooms or dwellings.
Ejectment between rival church-council factions over church property title; no letting/lodging issue.

Ordinary year-to-year house tenancy between father and son; dispute is purely procedural (magistrate jurisdiction requires 'a certain rent'), not about lodging, boarding, or short-term letting; no supporting quotes sought given irrelevance.
Interpleader dispute over ownership of a debt/fund; no relation to letting or lodging.
Replevin over a distrained corundum wheel; 'traveler's baggage at an inn' appears only as an illustrative aside on distress exemptions, not as a holding about lodging/innkeeping.

Misjoinder-of-parties dispute (life tenant and remainderman) over subsidence damage to a hotel property from coal mining; hotel mentioned only as the damaged asset, not litigated as a lodging/letting question.
Priority dispute between ground-rent judgment and a mortgage; no letting/lodging issue.
Testamentary charge/annuity dispute over Orphans' Court vs. equity jurisdiction; homestead-use provisions are family maintenance bequests, not compensated letting.
Trustee's accounting and distribution after partition sale among tenants in common; no letting/lodging issue.

new.court: Lehigh County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Accounting between tenants-in-common of a slate quarry for the value of mineral taken; 'tenant houses' on the property mentioned only in passing in fact findings.

new.court: Dauphin County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Motion to strike a mechanic's-lien judgment/sheriff's sale against a tenant's leasehold; no letting/lodging issue.

Municipal-nuisance tort case: plaintiff's ordinary monthly-rental houses were vacated/reduced in rent by a neighboring privy-well nuisance; the holding concerns city liability for nuisance, not the legal character of letting or lodging/boarding regulation.

new.court: Warren County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Oil-lease drainage/damages dispute; no letting/lodging issue.
Ejectment between two non-titled occupants of a vacant strip used for storing building materials; no letting/lodging issue.

Dispute over revocability of a parol license to use a stairway between two adjoining commercial/office buildings; tenants mentioned (secret societies, a newspaper company, a lawyer's office) are ordinary commercial-space lessees, not lodgers/boarders.
Equity bill to remove a narrow-gauge mining railroad built under a right-of-way grant; no letting/lodging issue.
Poor-law settlement dispute turning on a husband's curtesy interest in his wife's land where the family resided; not a compensated letting/lodging arrangement.

Procedural sufficiency of a landlord-and-tenant dispossession complaint (affidavit, sheriff's return, jury array) for a year-to-year tenement lease at $41.67/month; no facts about lodging/boarding or short-term room letting.
Ground-rent lease/Statute of Frauds and adverse-possession dispute over a lot originally under a 10,000-year ground lease; no lodging/boarding facts.
Oil lease/royalty dispute (mutual mistake as to well location) between lessors and oil-well lessees; no lodging/boarding facts.
Widow's dower action improperly amended into a debt action; a purely procedural real-property/pleading dispute with no lodging or short-term letting facts.
Ejectment service-of-process rule (service on tenant in possession after lease expiry); house and lot in Titusville, but no facts on lodging/boarding or short-term compensated occupancy.
Railroad condemnation/fixture-ownership dispute (whether rails/ties dedicated to landowner); wholly unrelated to lodging or dwelling letting.

Commercial building lease (Market street, $250/month, 3-year term) with partial eviction by paramount title; addresses rent apportionment doctrine, not lodging/boarding practice. who_was_letting/characterization noted from facts but no supporting quote extracted since not central to relevance determination.
Mortgage scire facias / breach-of-warranty-of-title damages dispute tied to a railroad's taking of part of the mortgaged premises; no lodging/boarding facts.
Guardian's authority to lease a minor ward's land for oil development without Orphans' Court approval; oil-and-mineral realty law, no lodging/boarding facts.

Dwelling-house leased for one year at $25/month to a tenant (Breuckmann) who occupied for the full family household, not as a lodger/boarder; dispute is over whether landlord accepted surrender of the lease upon repairs/re-entry. No lodging-house or boarding facts; ordinary whole-house tenancy.
Farm lease dispute over husbandry obligations (spreading lime, tillage custom); agricultural tenancy, no lodging/boarding facts.

new.court: Schuylkill County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Store and dwelling house in Port Carbon let at $250/year, then $90/year; dispute concerns whether a grantee of the landlord can proceed under the landlord-and-tenant dispossession act without attornment. Ordinary commercial/dwelling lease, no lodging/boarding facts.

new.court: Philadelphia County Court of Common Pleas
new.notes: Equity injunction denied against a landlord's statutory dispossession proceeding where defendants claimed to be vendees, not tenants; no lodging/boarding facts, purely a jurisdiction/remedy question.
Coal-mining trespass dispute over gangway boundary between surface owner and coal owner; wholly unrelated to lodging/room letting.
Criminal forcible-detainer indictment concerning a store-room leased to a milliner by the building owner; a commercial lease/criminal-pleading case, not lodging or boarding-house regulation.

Dispute over a landlord's statutory lien on improvements a lessee erected on a vacant lot, resolved via forcible entry and detainer proceedings; not about compensated occupancy of rooms/dwellings or lodging/boarding regulation.
Parol gift of farmland and statute-of-frauds/improvements dispute between family members; no letting, lodging, or boarding arrangement at issue.
Commercial storehouse lease between a lessor and a brewing association, dispute over holding over and option terms via subtenants; not residential letting or lodging.
Guardian's liability for farming his wards' land without a court order and ownership of resulting crops; no letting or lodging of dwellings involved.
Whether a commercial storefront leasehold with a sublet-consent clause is subject to attachment/execution; a business-lease creditor dispute, not residential lodging.

Adverse-possession/limitation dispute turning on whether a tenant's occupancy of a house and garden extends constructive possession to the whole tract; not about the legal character of letting or lodging.

Homestead-exemption/mortgage-lien dispute; passing mention that the family may have briefly lived on rented Dallas property while building a new home, but no facts on a landlord's letting practice, price, or lodging character.
Injunction against removal of fixtures a fair association's mechanics' lien creditors sought to sell off land leased for fairground use; not residential letting or lodging.
Married woman's defective deed acknowledgment, partition, and cotenant adverse-possession dispute over inherited land; no letting or lodging issue.
Party-wall cost-sharing contract and lien enforced against a homestead where the owner ran a saloon/restaurant; a commercial-building construction/lien dispute, not lodging.
Rural-vs-urban homestead-exemption dispute over a forty-acre farm partly within city limits; owner maintains a land-agency office in town, but nothing concerns letting rooms or lodging.
Complex equitable/legal-title priority dispute among land claimants and an administrator's sale; no letting or lodging of dwellings at issue.
Apportionment of farm rents between an old and new landlord after a partition sale of leased farmland; agricultural tenancy, not residential room letting or lodging.
Cotenant adverse-possession/limitation dispute over inherited land; no compensated occupancy or lodging arrangement.
Executory land-sale contract treated as creating a landlord-tenant-like relation pending payment, litigated over admissibility of a prior judgment; not a letting/lodging case.
Venue dispute over recovering warehouse storage fees for stored cotton seed; commercial warehousing, not residential letting or lodging.
Landlord's statutory lien on a tenant's cotton crop and pledge/attachment priority dispute; agricultural tenancy, not lodging or room letting.
Procedural forcible entry and detainer case holding rent not recoverable in that action; no lodging/boarding house or compensated-occupancy facts at issue.
Agricultural plantation sub-tenancy and landlord's distress-warrant lien dispute; no dwelling/lodging occupancy at issue.
General farm-premises subletting/assignment and trespass/conversion dispute; no lodging or boarding arrangement.
Suit for rent of a commercial store-house; pleading/estoppel issue only, no lodging or boarding facts.
Landlord's lien dispute over improvements on a leased pleasure-park lot; no residential lodging/boarding occupancy.

Sale-of-personal-property (whisky barrels) fraud/estoppel case; not about letting real property at all. Matched selector only on 'incident of ownership' language re: chattel possession, not dwelling letting.
Sub-tenant vs. assignee distinction over cotton crop rent claim on farmland; no dwelling/lodging occupancy.
Farmland rent suit; tenant-estoppel-from-disputing-landlord's-title doctrine. No lodging/boarding facts.
Mortgagee/rent-charge and homestead-descent dispute over farmland; no lodging or boarding-house occupancy.
Trespasser's claim to sugar cane grown on disputed-title land; use-and-occupation damages issue, not a letting arrangement.
Same sub-tenant/assignee-of-lease distinction as case_id 1368871, re-litigated on remand; farmland cotton crop, no dwelling occupancy.
Rent suit following a rescinded land-sale contract; no landlord-tenant relation found to exist, no lodging facts.
Landlord's statutory lien and right to sue out distress warrant over farm crops; no lodging or boarding occupancy.

Contract giving exclusive rent-free use of 100 acres of farmland (with some houses) for three years as security-for-reconveyance arrangement; forcible-detainer/estoppel holding. Agricultural tenancy, not compensated lodging/boarding.
Farmland lease/mortgage dispute with homestead and tenant-purchasing-outstanding-title issues; no lodging or boarding occupancy.
Farm lease-for-crop-share and landlord's statutory lien/trial-of-right-of-property dispute over cotton; no dwelling letting.
Land-grant citizenship/inheritance and partition dispute; no letting or lodging occupancy of any kind at issue.
Rent-holding-over dispute involving a leased livery stable (commercial business premises); not a residential lodging/boarding arrangement.
Suit for unpaid rent on farmland under a written tenancy contract; tenant-estoppel doctrine (tenant cannot dispute landlord's title). No bearing on lodging/boarding of dwellings or rooms.

Concerns municipal ordinance and jurisdiction over 'keeping disorderly houses' (houses of prostitution/assignation) under city charter/police power. This is vice regulation, not regulation of ordinary lodging or boarding houses; no discussion of compensated room/dwelling letting.
Trial of right of property dispute over a landlord's distress-warrant lien on goods in a commercial storehouse after tenant's attachment/sale. No dwelling or lodging occupancy at issue.
Contract dispute over sale of hay and claimed barn storage/rent charges. Involves 'rent' vs 'storage' distinction for goods, not occupancy of a dwelling or rooms by a person.
Constitutionality of an occupation tax on sellers of illustrated periodicals (Police News, Police Gazette). No connection to lodging, boarding, or dwelling occupancy.
Land title/limitations dispute; passing mention of a 'sojourner' who occupied vacant houses briefly as an uncompensated intruder with no claim of right. No compensated letting arrangement at issue.

Validity of a Sunday ordinance prohibiting liquor sales, applied to a brewery/tavern keeper. Concerns tavern/grog-shop licensing power and religious-liberty constitutional claims, not lodging or boarding of dwellings.
Tenants-in-common dispute over sale of a jointly owned slave; discusses tenancy-in-common and trover doctrine generally, unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

Liquor-license bond forfeiture case; licensee leased part of his grocery/tavern building to another to operate a billiard saloon, held to violate a no-gaming covenant. Concerns commercial premises leasing and gaming regulation, not dwelling lodging.
Forcible entry and detainer proceeding over town lots put into possession by sheriff's writ. No lodging/boarding arrangement involved.
Land title dispute turning on whether a conditional title bond satisfies the five-year limitations statute. No lodging/boarding issue.
Land grant title dispute involving alienage plea, a void 1839 judgment, and limitations by tenant possession. Passing reference to a 'tenant' cultivating land; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Equity dispute between tenants in common over one co-tenant's independent acquisition of a defective/outstanding land title. No lodging or dwelling-letting issue.
Lease of a steam saw mill (commercial machinery/equipment) and liability for its accidental destruction by fire; general lease-covenant construction. Not a dwelling/room lodging arrangement.
Municipal authority to grant a toll-bridge franchise; nuisance and ultra vires analysis of a city charter. No connection to lodging or boarding houses.

Married-woman's-acknowledgment/homestead deed-of-trust validity case. Facts recite in passing that the couple, after leaving their homestead, 'kept a boarding house' in several cities 'using rented houses all the while' — but the boarding-house operation is background biography, not adjudicated; the holding concerns deed acknowledgment formalities, not the legal character of lodging/boarding. Treated as passing mention per instructions.

Trial-of-right-of-property/execution dispute over cotton seized under attachment; counsel's brief draws an analogy to landlord distress-warrant/rent-replevy liens on crops, but no actual dwelling or lodging occupancy is at issue in this case.

Heir's sale of land interest and title-bond dispute; discusses tenant-estoppel doctrine as to a lease of land (Middleton's lease) merged into a purchased fee. No dwelling/room lodging arrangement at issue.

Land title/limitations dispute involving agricultural tenancy and estoppel of a tenant to deny landlord's title; no compensated occupancy of a dwelling/rooms at issue. Selector matched on unrelated tenant-estoppel language.
Suit on covenant of warranty of title to a city lot against a guardian; procedural/damages questions only. No lodging or room-letting facts.
Landlord's statutory right to reopen a trespass-to-try-title judgment entered against his tenants without notice; land occupancy, not compensated lodging/room letting.
Indictment for permitting card-playing at a 'saloon' (house for retailing spirituous liquors) quashed for indefinite description; concerns liquor/gaming regulation, not lodging or boarding houses.
Distress warrant dispute over crop-share rent (cotton/corn) under an agricultural plantation lease; not a dwelling/room letting arrangement.
Deed-construction/tenancy-in-common land title dispute over league grants; no lodging or room-letting facts.
Community-property partition suit over a surviving husband's power to sell real estate; unrelated to compensated lodging.
Procedural land-title dispute (parties pendente lite, description sufficiency); no dwelling-letting facts.
Trespass-to-try-title dispute among tenants in common over a headright survey; no lodging/room-letting facts.

Town ordinance abating a dilapidated former livery stable used as a public 'sink' as a nuisance, and voiding its summary sale/demolition; involves police-power nuisance abatement of a building but not lodging/boarding-house regulation.
Mortgage-note foreclosure and mistaken-description dispute; no lodging/room-letting facts.
Heirship/land-grant title dispute (colonial-era inheritance rules); no dwelling-letting facts.
Distress-warrant dispute over crop-share rent (cotton) under a plantation lease; agricultural, not dwelling/room letting.

Trespass-to-try-title/vendor's-lien dispute in which a landlord's statutory right to intervene for tenants is discussed; tenants held rented land under a landlord (Hamilton), not a lodging arrangement.
Municipal ordinance impounding/selling hogs running at large in city streets as a nuisance; a police-power/nuisance case but wholly unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.

Whether a cotton-warehousing/compress company's business is 'affected with a public interest' (public-use/monopoly doctrine); discusses public employments generally but the business itself is cotton storage, not lodging/boarding houses.

Forcible-entry-and-detainer/injunction dispute over title to a house and lot following execution sale; a tenant (Catharine Wilson) occupied the property and attorned to a new purchaser, but the case turns on title/procedure, not on the character or duration of a compensated lodging arrangement.
Trespass-to-try-title dispute among tenants in common/heirs, with limitations issues; no dwelling-letting facts.
Guardian-and-ward accounting case; guardian occupied ward's homestead in lieu of separate maintenance allowance. No compensated lodger/boarder arrangement at issue.
Landlord's statutory lien on a merchant-tenant's store goods for unpaid commercial store rent; no dwelling/lodging occupancy at issue.
Land title dispute over breach of covenant of right to sell/warranty; involves ouster by a paramount titleholder, not any lodging or letting arrangement.
Mechanic's/materialman's lien dispute over money loaned for homestead construction materials; no letting or lodging arrangement involved.
Fixtures dispute over ownership of a bank safe and vault sold with a building; no residential letting or lodging at issue.
Land purchase/warranty covenant dispute involving eviction by a superior title; wife's equitable interest in land bought with separate funds. No lodging/letting issue.
Malicious-prosecution suit over a stolen dog; that Weisensee 'was keeping a boarding-house' and some boarders left is a passing background fact, not a holding on lodging/letting law.

Suit for specific performance of a parol land-sale contract; that plaintiff rented houses he built on the lot to a Mrs. Terrell is incidental to establishing possession/value, not a holding on lodging characterization.
Community-property/limitations title dispute over a league grant; placing 'tenants' on the land was to perfect adverse-possession limitation title, not compensated dwelling occupancy.
Mortgagor/mortgagee dispute over construction of a 'free of rent' possession clause in a mortgage; not a lodging or room-letting arrangement.
Procedural opinion explaining the new Supreme Court briefing rules; underlying dispute involves tenant possession of agricultural land for limitations purposes, not lodging/boarding.
Public-land pre-emption/settler statute dispute over a sawmill site; concerns actual-settler residency requirements for purchasing public domain, not lodging houses.
Fixtures dispute over ownership of a sugar-mill sold with a plantation; unrelated to residential letting or lodging.
Trespass-to-try-title case turning on privity of successive adverse possessors of a tract (settlers who lived there); not a compensated lodging/boarding arrangement.
Mortgage-foreclosure case addressing a commercial/business lessee's (five-year term, brick building improvements) right to redeem as a necessary party; not a short-term dwelling lodging arrangement.
Tax dispute over liquor-license and jail/courthouse levies; no lodging-house licensing or letting issue.
City fire-limits ordinance banning wooden buildings, struck down as ultra vires under the nuisance-abatement power; concerns building materials, not lodging/boarding-house licensing.
Accounting dispute between tenants in common over profits from a commercial railroad-iron storage business on co-owned lots; not a residential lodging/letting arrangement.
Trespass to try title / partition pleading and heirship-evidence dispute; no letting of rooms or dwellings at issue.
Farm plantation lease/sublease and distress-warrant dispute between landlord and agricultural tenant; not dwelling/lodging letting.
Trespass to try title turning on adverse possession and tenancy-for-limitation-purposes doctrine as to farmland; no lodging/boarding facts.
Trespass to try title dispute over rents and value of improvements on a town lot; no lodging or boarding arrangement.
Trespass/forcible-ejectment damages case; plaintiff built a bar and restaurant on leased lot, a commercial venture, not a lodging/room-letting arrangement.
Equity partition suit over a large land grant involving mortgagor/mortgagee-like interests and reconvention; no letting of a dwelling for occupancy.
Dispute over implied vs. limited warranty in a deed of partition among co-tenants of a land grant; no dwelling-letting facts.
Multi-year commercial house lease dispute over delayed delivery of possession and estoppel; term is years, not short-term lodging, and no facts on rooms/boarders.
Distress-warrant/reconvention dispute between landlord and cotton/corn cropper tenant; agricultural rent dispute, not dwelling letting.

Family partition/community-property suit; mentions co-tenant renting common property to third persons in passing, but no facts on householder letting of a dwelling for lodging.

Quo warranto over a ship-channel toll franchise and municipal bond/contract validity; unrelated to dwelling letting or lodging-house regulation.
County commissioners' authority to issue bonds for a courthouse; no dwelling-letting or lodging-regulation content.

Land-title limitation dispute turning on tenant attornment doctrine; concerns farmland possession, not room/dwelling lodging.

Dispute over priority between a landlord's statutory lien and a chattel mortgage on billiard tables in a month-to-month commercial store-house tenancy; no household lodging/boarding issue.
Adverse possession of a town street fenced by permission of town council; landlord/tenant relation invoked only by analogy to permissive possession, not household letting.
Mortgagor/mortgagee rights to ungathered crops on farm land worked under a farming partnership/tenancy; agricultural rent law, no household lodging issue.
Trespass-to-try-title dispute among tenants in common over land and joint liability of co-defendants for rents/waste; no lodging or boarding issue.
Constitutional/statutory construction of county authority to levy a special tax for building an addition to a courthouse; unrelated to letting or lodging.
Adverse possession/limitation dispute between tenants in common claiming land by heirship; no household letting or boarding issue.

Privity of contract/estate between landlord and sub-tenant on a farm as to landlord's distress-warrant remedy against sub-tenant's crops; agricultural rent law, no household lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: A city ordinance made it a criminal offense to rent, let or lease any premises within the city limits to a prostitute or lewd woman, without regard to the use to which the premises were put; the mayor was removed from office by the city aldermen for renting a house to such a woman. The Texas Supreme Court held the ordinance null and void as an unreasonable, proscriptive denial of shelter to an 'unfortunate class' and in contravention of common right, and accordingly voided the mayor's removal.

quotes.text: any person who shall knowingly furnish, rent, let or lease any premises or place within the city Emits to any prostitute or lewd woman, or to any person for their use, shaU be deemed guilty of an offense.

That unfortunate and degraded class against whom the ordinance was mainly intended, however far they may have fallen beneath the true mission of women, which it is one oh our highest duties to foster and protect in social and domestic life, are still human beings, entitled to shelter and the protection of the law; and the council did not have the power to so far proscribe them as a class, as to make it a penal offense in any one to rent them a habitation without regard to its use.
Such an ordinance is null and void, because unreasonable and in contravention of common right.

new.notes: Favorable on the level-of-generality point: the court strikes down a municipal attempt to criminalize renting property to a disfavored class of occupant, treating the right to let a habitation as protected regardless of the letter's identity or purpose. The opinion never specifies whether Milliken owned/occupied the house himself or as pure investment property, nor the term of the tenancy, so who_was_letting and duration_of_occupancy are left unclear; characterization left null because the court addresses the ordinance's validity, not whether the arrangement was a lease/license/lodging.

Interstate commerce / police power case about a statutory penalty for a railway's refusal to deliver freight on tender of bill-of-lading charges. No occupancy or lodging issue; 'police power' matter is freight regulation, not boarding-house regulation.

new.holding_summary: In a homestead-exemption dispute, the court held that when an owner permanently devotes part of his town homestead lot to houses built and rented out for income, that portion ceases to be exempt homestead, even though the parcel was never formally subdivided; the owner's undisputed practice of renting rooms/houses to a boarding-house keeper and then to a succession of monthly tenants was treated throughout as an ordinary, unquestioned exercise of ownership.

new.notes: Marginal call: the actual holding is homestead-abandonment doctrine, not the legality/character of letting itself. Included because the owner's practice of renting his old residence to a boarding-house keeper (he then boarded with her) and building a second house purely to rent for income is never questioned as unlawful -- courts treat it as an unremarkable incident of ownership, only debating its homestead consequence. Court never classifies the arrangement as lease/license/lodging, so characterization left null. 'boarded with her' is an existing lexicon term, not new.

new.holding_summary: The court held that an unoccupied guest room in a hotel/tavern remains part of the public house, and thus a 'public place' under the anti-gambling statute, until a guest actually appropriates it as a temporary lodging or residence. Because the defendant and others used an unoccupied guest room only to play cards rather than to lodge in it, the room was not a private room exempt from the statute, and the card-playing conviction was affirmed.

quotes.text: an inn, tavern or hotel means a place for the general entertainment and lodging of all travelers and strangers who apply, paying suitable compensation, A hotel “guest” is one who lives at board or lodging in a hired room, and “lodging” is a place of rest for a night, or a residence for a time— a temporary habitation.

new.holding_summary: In a burglary prosecution, where a house had two rooms separated by a partition and the alleged owner rented the whole house but let the other room to a subtenant, the room she occupied and exclusively controlled was properly alleged as her 'house.' The court treated the sub-letting arrangement as an ordinary tenancy that did not create joint ownership of either room.

quotes.text: The entire house had been rented by Amanda Isom, and Lula Smith was her tenant of one of the rooms.

new.holding_summary: A club had rented a lake-front 'camp' from its owner for several months; when a member helping remove property after the tenancy ended was injured by a rotten wharf stringer, the court held the owner liable, since a lessor is bound to know whether the premises he lets are safe and must answer in damages to anyone lawfully thereon injured by a defect, whether from original construction or failure to repair.

quotes.text: The owner is‘bound to know whether his building is safe for the purposes for which he rents it, or authorizes its use, or is rotten and unsafe, and is answerable, in damages, to those who, being lawfully therein, are injured by reason of its defects, whether of original construction or caused by failure to make proper repairs.

new.holding_summary: An elderly roomer who rented a room from defendant at $1 per week, and who fell after a defective door knob parted from the door, could not recover damages, because under ordinary Louisiana landlord-tenant law such minor repairs are by law the tenant's own responsibility, not the landlord's, even though she was unaware of the defect.

quotes.text: She had been renting a room from defendant at the rate of $1 per week, and she relates in her petition that, while occupying said room,

Such repairs are by law imposed upon the tenant and not upon the landlord, and plaintiff is in no position to seek damages for their nonperformance, even though she had not been aware of their necessity.

Such repairs are by law imposed upon the tenant and not upon the landlord, and plaintiff is in no position to seek damages for their nonperformance, even though she had not been aware of their necessity.

new.notes: Defendant had at least one other tenant (Robert Jackson) in the same building whom she instructed to make repairs for plaintiff, suggesting a multi-room rooming arrangement rather than a single householder letting a spare room, hence coded commercial_operator; marked favorable because the court treats weekly-rate room letting as an unremarkable, lawful tenancy governed by ordinary landlord-tenant law rather than as suspect or restricted, notwithstanding the plaintiff losing on the repair-duty issue.
Streetcar one-man-car safety ordinance under police power; no dwelling-letting issue.

Parish cattle-tick-dipping ordinance under police power; unrelated to dwelling-letting.
Oyster-bedding-ground lease criminal statute construction; unrelated to dwelling-letting.

Jurisdictional dispute over ejectment of a commercial store lessee and tacit reconduction of a store lease; ordinary/yearly commercial lease, not short-term dwelling letting.

new.holding_summary: Where one, assuming the character of tenant, without the consent of the owner, enters upon premises which are unfit for occupancy and undergoing repairs, including the repairing of plaster upon walls and ceilings saturated and loosened by stormwater, he assumes the risks incidental to such repairs, and, among them, the risk of falling plaster.

quotes.text: Where one, assuming the character of tenant, without the consent of the owner, enters upon premises which are unfit for occupancy and undergoing repairs, including the repairing of plaster upon walls and ceilings saturated and loosened by stormwater, he assumes the risks incidental to such repairs, and, among them, the risk of falling plaster.

new.notes: Background facts describe an individual owner routinely letting portions of a double tenement cottage to paying tenants by the month as an ordinary matter, unremarked by the court -- consistent with letting as an ordinary incident of ownership; but the actual holding turns on assumption of risk for an unauthorized entrant, not on a formal lease/license characterization, so characterization is left null. Plaintiff's own occupancy at the dwelling in question ran roughly six weeks (mid-November to late December) before the injury, hence 'weeks' rather than the background monthly rental figure.
Year-long residential lease to two co-lessees; dispute is over the several (not solidary) liability of the co-lessees for rent notes, not short-term letting or lodging.

Priority dispute among vendor's-privilege and lessor's-privilege creditors over barroom fixtures sold at sheriff's sale; no lodging content.
Lessee's duty of care to guard a leased dwelling at termination (liability for stolen gas fixtures after vacating without notice); ordinary residential lease, not short-term letting.
Rent/trespass claim over unopened pasture squares used to graze cattle; no dwelling letting or lodging issue.
Possession dispute in which the defendant's alleged lease of the property was found unproven; no lodging or short-term letting content.
Petitory action over boundary lines and an alleged servitude of passage; no letting or lodging content.

Quantum meruit claim for services rendered plus a manual-gift claim against a succession; the statement that claimant 'formerly kept a boarding house where the decedent... took his meals and paid her for them' is a passing background detail establishing the parties' relationship, not adjudicated or discussed further -- excluded per the passing-mention rule.
Commercial lease of theater building canceled after fire marshal ordered closure for inadequate exits; landlord-tenant repair/vice-and-defect dispute, no bearing on lodging/boarding.

Privilege/lien dispute over unpaid charges for watching wharf-stored cargo; no residential letting or lodging content.

Homestead patent/title dispute between a homesteader and a railroad's grantee; no letting or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: A landlord sued a married-woman tenant for unpaid rent on a three-year lease of two New Orleans residences. The court held her Missouri domicile gave her capacity to contract and be sued as a feme sole without her husband joined, and affirmed judgment for the rent with recognition of the landlord's lien on the leased property. The case treats the residential lease itself as an ordinary, valid, enforceable contract; the actual dispute concerns the tenant's capacity/domicile, not the character of the letting.

quotes.text: the plaintiff leased to Mrs. Alice A. Taylor, the defendant herein, the two residences, known as “1519 and 1525 Joseph Street,” in the city of New Orleans, for the term of three years

The district court rendered judgment in favor of the plaintiff against the defendant for $1,150, with interest thereon, for $115 attorney’s fees, with recognition and maintenance of plaintiff’s landlord’s lien and privilege on the property leased.

The district court rendered judgment in favor of the plaintiff against the defendant for $1,150, with interest thereon, for $115 attorney’s fees, with recognition and maintenance of plaintiff’s landlord’s lien and privilege on the property leased.

Will-nullity/concubinage succession dispute; a private boarding house in Cincinnati is mentioned only in passing as a travel lodging, not as the subject of any holding on letting or regulation.

new.holding_summary: Plaintiff leased a room opening onto a gallery from defendant; the gallery railing gave way while plaintiff was moving out, injuring him. The court held a lessor is as much bound to keep the necessary approaches to leased rooms/apartments safe for ordinary use as the apartments themselves, but ultimately found the tenant's own misuse of the railing (lowering furniture over it) was not the ordinary use the lessor warranted, and reversed the judgment for plaintiff.

quotes.text: The lessor, we think, is as much bound for the safety, for ordinary use, of the necessary approaches and exits to and from the apartments which he lets as for the safety of the apartments themselves.

new.holding_summary: Dispute over the nature of an oil and gas lease/contract and rights of locators under federal placer mining law; oil and gas leases held distinct from ordinary farm or house leases.

new.holding_summary: Mortgage on co-owners' undivided interest in land attaches to the specific tract allotted on partition; such a partition-attachment clause is valid and not void for uncertainty.
new.notes: Mortgage/partition law dispute among heirs; no occupancy-for-pay or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: Petitory action by landowner against a five-year agricultural tenant who refused to pay rent and disputed her title; tenant estopped from denying landlord's title while in possession, and tenant's improvements are liable for arrears of rent.
new.notes: A multi-year agricultural land lease dispute (tenant estoppel, rent arrears), not compensated occupancy of a dwelling/rooms; no lodging, boarding, or short-term letting facts.

new.holding_summary: An open-air dancing pavilion in a private amusement park operated for profit is not a 'dance hall' requiring neighboring property owners' consent under the city charter's licensing provision for barrooms, saloons, and dance halls.

new.holding_summary: Jurisdictional and injunction dispute arising from mortgage foreclosure over timberland; court where mortgagor is domiciled has jurisdiction over an in personam suit and may enjoin destruction of mortgaged property even though the property lies elsewhere.

new.holding_summary: In a succession partition, a minor who resides with his mother in a co-owned house is not personally liable to his co-owner sister for rent; if anyone is liable it is the mother who occupied the property, and a minor's capital cannot be charged with rent absent a family meeting and court authorization.
new.notes: Family co-owners occupying their own inherited house, not a third party paying to occupy another's dwelling; rent dispute is among co-heirs, not a lodging/letting arrangement.

new.holding_summary: A materialman's lien for lumber used to build a house on another's land properly attaches to the house itself, even though title to the house passed to a purchaser; the builder occupied the land as a tenant at will/sufferance of the landowner.
new.notes: Mechanic's-lien dispute over a house built with landowner's consent; 'tenant at will' language describes possession of a building lot, not compensated occupancy of a dwelling by a lodger/boarder.

new.holding_summary: A tutor lacked authority to convey a minor's interest in land to attorneys as a fee absent public auction as required by Civil Code art. 341; a statute permitting attorneys to contract for a fee interest in litigated property does not impliedly repeal that requirement for minors.
new.notes: Minors' tutorship/sale-of-land case; no occupancy or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: Mayor lacked authority to suppress exhibition of prize-fight films absent an ordinance actually in evidence; exception of no cause of action improperly sustained because such ordinances cannot be judicially noticed and must be proven on the merits.
new.notes: Movie-theater licensing/censorship dispute; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: Grantee of a municipal right-of-way/switch-track privilege cannot recover 'rent' from a party who tortiously uses that right of way, since no landlord-tenant relation exists, but may recover tort damages measured by rental value, subject to one-year prescription.
new.notes: Railroad right-of-way/switch-track franchise dispute; 'landlord and tenant' analysis is used only to reject a rent claim over street usage, not dwelling occupancy.

new.holding_summary: Adjoining landowner (a hotel company) and its contractor held solidarily liable in tort for construction damage (excavation, pile driving) to a neighboring building; damages measured by cost of restoration.
new.notes: Construction-damage tort suit between adjoining landowners; the defendant happens to be a hotel company, but the case does not address the legal character of guest/lodger occupancy.

new.holding_summary: Members of a hunting/fishing club acquired ownership of land by 30 years' adverse possession as joint tenants/co-owners, without need of title or good faith.
new.notes: Adverse-possession dispute over club-owned hunting land; no compensated occupancy or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: Co-owner's acquisition of a tax title to co-owned land inures to the benefit of all co-owners; a later relinquishment made expressly 'as heir' does not convey the co-owner's separate tax-title interest to a third party.
new.notes: Title dispute among heirs/co-owners over land ownership; no dwelling-letting or lodging facts.

new.holding_summary: In a boundary/title dispute, a specific metes-and-bounds description in a deed controls over a general acreage reference, and a bona fide third-party purchaser's recorded title prevails over an unrecorded claim based on acreage discrepancy.
new.notes: Land title/description and registry-notice dispute; no occupancy-for-pay issue.

new.holding_summary: Injunction denied because plaintiff failed to prove dedication of a private plat's streets to public use in a sparsely settled, largely fictional 'village'; the mere existence of a plat naming streets is insufficient proof of dedication.
new.notes: Street-dedication/injunction dispute between two adjoining landowners; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.
Petitory action over land title/a purported lease to a gin company; dispute is about ownership and bad-faith possession, not compensated occupancy of a dwelling.

Negligence pleading case about a woman injured by a defective stable door while storing furniture; a tenant is mentioned but the holding is purely about pleading sufficiency, not lodging/letting doctrine.
Lease voided as let for prostitution outside the city's restricted vice district; concerns regulation of vice, not boarding/lodging-house letting or short-term room letting by a householder.
Community-property partition dispute over paving liens, attorney fees, and a wife's occupancy of the former marital home in lieu of alimony; not a compensated third-party letting arrangement.

new.holding_summary: In a succession partition, the court credited defendant, who lived in and helped support the family home, with the value of a dwelling she built there, financing it in part with her earnings as a laundress and from taking in boarders and lodgers; that credit fully offset her coheirs' claim for rental value of her occupancy.

quotes.text: she worked as a laundress, and had boarders and lodgers on the premises, for whom she did the cooking.
she worked as a laundress, and had boarders and lodgers on the premises, for whom she did the cooking.
We are therefore of the opinion that the claim for rents made by plaintiffs should be compensated in full by the value of this improvement.

new.notes: Boarding/lodging is incidental factual background (source of the defendant's income) rather than a litigated legal characterization, but the court treats a householder's taking in of paying boarders/lodgers as ordinary, legitimate income-generating activity.
Police-power case about a city ordering removal of railway bridge piers obstructing a street; no connection to residential letting or lodging houses.
Mandamus dispute over transfer of pledged corporate stock certificates; a cited precedent mentions rental value of stock, unrelated to real property letting.

Slander-of-title suit over a restrictive covenant requiring a 'single residence'; court holds the covenant merely personal, allowing construction of a triplex apartment house. Concerns real-obligation/covenant doctrine for multi-unit construction, not compensated short-term room/lodging letting or its regulation.

Upholds ordinance requiring movers to report household-goods relocations to police, under the police power; regulates furniture haulers for anti-theft/surveillance purposes, not lodging or boarding houses.
Boundary-line/servitude dispute between adjoining lot owners; no letting or lodging issue present.

new.holding_summary: A landlord who locked a tenant out of leased rooms and seized his belongings without resort to legal process, rather than proceeding by law to regain possession, is liable in damages for the illegal, self-help ejectment.

quotes.text: The plaintiff alleges that he leased two rooms and a kitchen at No. 1112 Frenchmen Street from the defendants for $8 a month and resided there with his wife and family for more than a year prior to March 4, 1922
A landlord has no right to obtain possession of leased premises by ejecting the tenants without resorting to the means provided by law.
A landlord has no right to obtain possession of leased premises by ejecting the tenants without resorting to the means provided by law.

new.notes: Ordinary letting of two rooms and a kitchen from a householder, treated by the court as a straightforward lease/tenancy and protected against the landlord's illegal self-help eviction.
Suit for the value of a horse illegally sold by a constable; a pleading/exception ruling with no connection to property letting.
Suit on a release bond after provisional seizure of farm livestock/crops for unpaid rent under an agricultural lease; not a dwelling/room-letting or lodging-house case.
Mandamus over a suspensive appeal in an ejectment suit concerning a farm tract lease; procedural landlord-tenant dispute unrelated to dwelling/room letting or lodging-house doctrine.
Mechanic's lien/prescription dispute between a materialman and a homeowner over unpaid construction materials; no letting or lodging issue.
Trespass suit against road contractors and a police jury for damaging enclosed farmland while hauling gravel; unrelated to residential letting.

Personal-injury suit by sub-tenants against their sub-lessor and the building's purported owner over a collapsed gallery railing; a sublease is mentioned incidentally, but the holding concerns repair-duty/negligence liability, not the character or legality of the letting itself.

Negligence suit over collapsed steps at a leased dwelling; turns entirely on proof of who owned/leased the premises (defendant company shown not to be lessor), not on the character of a lodging/letting arrangement.
Ordinary 12-month house lease; suit for unpaid rent notes and rule-for-judgment procedure. No lodging/boarding/short-term letting issue.
Commercial retail-grocery lease use-restriction dispute (lunch/coffee/cold-drink stand). No occupancy-of-dwelling or lodging issue.
Real-estate-broker commission dispute; the property sold happens to be a 'rooming-house' but the case is about brokerage licensing, not the letting arrangement itself. Passing mention only.
Community-property mortgage/vendor's-privilege and subrogation dispute over sale of a lot. No occupancy-for-pay issue.
Building-materials lien suit and First City Court jurisdiction over lien enforcement. No occupancy or lodging issue.
Lease of a hotel building; dispute is purely lessor's-lien-vs-chattel-mortgage priority ranking on furniture. Hotel operation is incidental backdrop, not adjudicated as a letting-doctrine question.
Verbal lease of 203 acres of farmland; dispute over rent note and tenant improvements. No dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.
Commercial candy-kitchen store lease; reconduction and chattel-mortgage-vs-landlord's-lien priority. No lodging/dwelling issue.
Farm-labor share-crop ownership/privilege dispute over cotton. No occupancy-of-dwelling issue.
Ordinary one-year apartment lease rent dispute after eviction by rule to vacate; issue is scope of accrued-rent liability, not the legal character of the letting.
Tort suit over defective steps; question is whether a tenant's live-in paramour was 'lawfully on the premises,' not the legal character of compensated occupancy. No pay-for-occupancy issue litigated.
Ordinary residential lease rent dispute following statutory eviction for non-payment. No lodging/boarding issue.
Ordinary three-year apartment lease; dispute over abandonment, landlord's re-letting duty, and damage to premises. No lodging/short-term letting doctrine at issue.
Petitory land-title action requiring joinder of co-possessors. No occupancy-for-pay issue.
Streetcar-negligence personal injury suit; plaintiff's prior boarding-house income is mentioned only to establish lost earnings/damages. Passing mention, not adjudicated.
Commercial restaurant/soft-drink business lease with equipment; dispute over abandonment, mitigation, and rent. No dwelling/lodging occupancy issue.
Tenant's negligence suit against landlord for falling plaster; a boarder present at the scene is mentioned incidentally as a witness. Case concerns repair duty under Art. 2716, not lodging doctrine.
Suit by property purchaser against tenant for unpaid rent and ejectment procedure; no lodging/boarding-house issue, ordinary landlord-tenant/ejectment dispute.

Innkeeper's statutory liability cap for lost guest baggage (C.C. art. 2971); hotel-guest relationship assumed, not adjudicated, and case does not address duration, characterization, or lawfulness of letting rooms.

Domicile/candidacy dispute; boarding house mentioned only in a quoted passage on domicile doctrine (residing in a hotel or boarding house doesn't defeat residency), not the subject of adjudication here.

new.holding_summary: In a dispute over a promise of sale, the court held Mrs. McCarty retained possession under the contract despite an intervening fire, entitling her to specific performance upon payment of the balance due. The property being purchased was contemplated to be occupied by her as a residence and also used by her for taking in boarders and roomers, though the court did not adjudicate the legal character of any boarding arrangement.

quotes.text: She further alleges that there was a dwelling house on the property which, under the contract, was to be occupied by her and her family as a residence, and also to be used by her for the purpose of taking boarders and roomers.

She further alleges that there was a dwelling house on the property which, under the contract, was to be occupied by her and her family as a residence, and also to be used by her for the purpose of taking boarders and roomers.

She further alleges that there was a dwelling house on the property which, under the contract, was to be occupied by her and her family as a residence, and also to be used by her for the purpose of taking boarders and roomers.

new.notes: Boarding is only background fact describing intended property use in a sale contract; case's actual holding concerns possession, payment timing, and insurance proceeds, not the boarding arrangement itself. characterization left null because the court never classifies the boarder/roomer arrangement.
Ordinary residential lease dispute over unpaid rent and leaky-roof damages to furniture; no boarding/lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: The court held that money earned by a wife operating a boarding house during the existence of the community fell into the community of acquets and gains, absent proof she operated it separate from her husband, making the property purchased with those earnings, and its rents, subject to seizure for community debts.

quotes.text: the proof shows that whatever consideration she paid for it was derived from operating a boarding house her earnings in which belonged to. the community between herself and her husband.
the proof shows that whatever consideration she paid for it was derived from operating a boarding house her earnings in which belonged to. the community between herself and her husband.

new.notes: Case treats boarding-house-keeping as an ordinary lawful business generating community earnings; does not address duration of occupancy of boarders or characterize the lodger relationship, so those fields are unclear/null.
Sale-of-goods case concerning delivery, bills of lading, and passage of title to a shipment of peaches; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.
Suit on a promissory note arising from a bond-for-deed land sale contract with racially restrictive covenants; no boarding/lodging issue.
Ordinary apartment lease dispute over landlord's unlawful entry and cancellation of lease; not a lodging or boarding-house arrangement.
Dispute between step-relatives over reimbursement for repairs/improvements and rent owed on a residence; ordinary tenancy, not boarding/lodging.
Trespass/damages suit over a furniture dealer's unauthorized repossession of goods from plaintiff's home; unrelated to letting or lodging.

new.holding_summary: The court found that plaintiff had leased a room in defendant's house for six months at $25 per month but occupied and paid rent for only three months, entitling defendant to two months' additional rent with recognition of his lessor's privilege on plaintiff's property, while rejecting defendant's speculative consequential-damages claims.

quotes.text: The preponderance of the evidence establishes that plaintiff leased a room in defendant’s house for six months at $25 a month and occupied and paid rent therefor only during three months.
The preponderance of the evidence establishes that plaintiff leased a room in defendant’s house for six months at $25 a month and occupied and paid rent therefor only during three months.
The preponderance of the evidence establishes that plaintiff leased a room in defendant’s house for six months at $25 a month and occupied and paid rent therefor only during three months.

new.notes: Householder let a room in his own dwelling to a lodger/tenant for pay, enforced by the court via recognition of the lessor's privilege; a clean incident-of-ownership case.
Agricultural farm-lease priority dispute involving unrecorded leases and a seizing creditor; unrelated to lodging or letting of rooms/dwellings.
Trapping-rights lease dispute over defective title to land; no relation to lodging/boarding.
Commercial dispute over yard/wharfage charges for use of shipyard facilities to repair a boat; unrelated to residential letting.

Dispute over return of a real-estate purchase deposit and a reconventional rent claim based on storing salvaged building materials in the yard of prospective purchase property; no occupancy of dwelling by a lodger/boarder.

Real-estate broker's commission dispute over sale of a proposed municipal tourist-camp site to the City of Shreveport; concerns a public campground/park site, not a private lodging or boarding-house practice. Selector 'tourist-home' appears to be a false positive here.
Priority dispute between a chattel mortgagee and a landlord's lien over household furniture in a furnished residential lease; ordinary residential tenancy, not a boarding/lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Commercial lease dispute over a skating rink's use of a hall (eviction defense and improvements/fixture reconvention); affirms rent judgment, amends award for a removable iron railing.
new.notes: Commercial building lease/eviction and fixtures dispute between a corporation and a skating rink company; no dwelling, lodging, or boarding-house issue.

new.holding_summary: Suit on promissory notes; exception to venue overruled on finding of defendant's domicile despite alternating residence between two towns.
new.notes: Personal domicile determination for venue purposes (defendant lived at property 'as an invited guest'); no compensated occupancy or lodging arrangement at issue.

new.holding_summary: Mandamus proceeding over third-possessor improvements (an irrigation canal) made under an agreement to rent land at a fair rental value; company held not a good-faith possessor entitled to reimbursement from the mortgagee.
new.notes: Agricultural land rental/improvements and mortgage foreclosure priority dispute; no dwelling or lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Tax situs dispute over a foreign insurance company's Louisiana loan notes; statute taxing such credits held constitutional.
new.notes: Corporate taxation of credits/notes; no relation to dwellings, lodging, or boarding.

new.holding_summary: Insanity commitment proceeding reversed because the statute applies only to state residents/citizens, and defendant's brief stay in the parish was temporary.
new.notes: Residency determination for interdiction/commitment jurisdiction; no compensated occupancy or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: Specific performance suit compelling an adjudicatee to accept title from a succession partition sale; family meeting and prescription/absentee-heir defenses rejected.
new.notes: Succession partition and title dispute; no dwelling occupancy, lodging, or boarding issue.

new.holding_summary: Conviction for maintaining a 'blind tiger' liquor nuisance reversed; the police-jury ordinance was superseded by a later, ex post facto statute.
new.notes: Liquor-nuisance ('blind tiger') criminal prosecution under a police-jury ordinance; not a lodging/boarding-house regulation.

new.holding_summary: Possessory action over an oil-and-gas lease; contract with delay-rental and cancellation clauses held not void, so lessee's possession under it defeats owner's possessory claim.
new.notes: Mineral/oil-and-gas lease validity and possessory-action pleading rules; unrelated to dwelling occupancy or lodging.

new.holding_summary: Separation from bed and board granted on grounds of excesses and cruel treatment, with defamation (spreading rumors of wife's insanity) as contributing evidence.
new.notes: Marital separation ('bed and board') case; unrelated to letting of rooms/dwellings despite phrase overlap with the corpus's search terms.

new.holding_summary: Conviction for keeping a 'blind tiger' reversed; police jury lacked authority to enact the liquor-keeping ordinance absent a voter-approved regulation.
new.notes: Liquor-nuisance prosecution and police jury's regulatory authority; not a lodging/boarding-house case.

new.holding_summary: Party-wall reimbursement dispute between adjoining Canal Street property owners; defendant owes half the reconstruction cost.
new.notes: Party-wall construction cost dispute; no occupancy, lodging, or letting issue.

new.holding_summary: State board of health held to have jurisdiction, concurrent with New Orleans's local board, to enjoin an unsanitary bakery as a public-health nuisance.
new.notes: Police-power/public-health regulation case, but the regulated business is a bakery, not a lodging or boarding house; outside corpus scope.

new.holding_summary: Continuation of a family partition/accounting suit; rents and disbursements between mother and daughter co-owners recast per prior appellate ruling.
new.notes: Accounting for rents among family co-owners of inherited property; not a compensated lodging/letting arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Railroad enjoined from letting its depot-ground warehouse be used for a lessee's private business, as the deed restricted use to railroad purposes.
new.notes: Deed-restriction dispute over railroad warehouse/depot grounds leased for grain storage; not dwelling occupancy or lodging.

new.holding_summary: Heirs' suit to recover community-property land rejected on grounds of prior settlement, dation en paiement, and 10/30-year prescription.
new.notes: Community-property title and prescription dispute; no occupancy, lodging, or letting issue.

new.holding_summary: Assault-and-battery damages suit against a town marshal who beat a baker with a pistol while quelling a disturbance among the baker's after-hours guests; damages increased against the marshal.
new.notes: Baker entertaining friends at his shop, and their sobriety/noise under municipal ordinances, is not compensated lodging; case is a false-arrest/assault tort, not a letting arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Retail-liquor license claims against an interstate brewer; 1898 general license law inapplicable to interstate commerce, but the 1908 Gay-Shattuck Act's police-power license upheld.
new.notes: Liquor licensing and interstate commerce/Wilson Act analysis; unrelated to dwelling lodging or boarding houses.

new.holding_summary: Certified questions on procedure for landlord eviction suits under Act 313 of 1908: appeal delay runs from oral rendition of judgment, judgments must be signed in open court, and eviction becomes executory 24 hours after rendition absent a suspensive appeal.
new.notes: General landlord-tenant summary eviction procedure applicable to any house/store/land lease; no facts about a householder letting rooms or a lodging/boarding arrangement, so it addresses the ordinary landlord-tenant regime rather than the corpus's specific practice.

Commercial building lease dispute (barroom/restaurant/boarding-house uses, liquor prohibition, fire damage, partnership liability); boarding-house use mentioned only in passing as one of several tenant uses, not adjudicated.
Community-property/estoppel dispute over a plantation sale-with-lease-option contract; no lodging or room-letting issue.

Simms leased a building and operated it 'as a cheap hotel or rooming house,' but the litigation concerns his eviction as lessee, an alleged conspiracy, and a fire-marshal demolition order -- the legal character of the lodging business itself is not adjudicated.
Church-property trespass/ownership dispute among trustees; no lodging issue.

Homestead-exemption case for a widow supporting her adult daughters; a boarding-house-keeping widow appears only in a distinguished citation (Whyte v. Grant), a different case's facts, not Mrs. Gow's.
Zoning-nuisance injunction against a grocery store operating in a residential district; no lodging/boarding issue.
Stock/no-fence-law election dispute; no lodging issue.
Zoning-nuisance injunction against a drug store operating in a residential district; no lodging/boarding issue.
Taxpayer injunction suit over levee-board construction-zone sequencing on a lakefront reclamation project; no lodging issue.
Ejectment appeal dismissed on procedural/jurisdictional grounds (wrong appeal bond, amount not shown); no lodging issue reached.

new.holding_summary: Plaintiffs' family sub-let and occupied a room in a house owned by defendant, and their child was injured falling through an unfastened window screen; the appellate court affirmed judgment for the owner-defendant, holding that under Civil Code article 2716 the duty to fasten and maintain window screens falls on the tenant/occupant, not the owner.

quotes.text: Mrs. Sledge sublet a part of the leased premises, which included the room in which the window in question was located, to the plaintiffs
Mrs. Sledge sublet a part of the leased premises, which included the room in which the window in question was located, to the plaintiffs
It was the duty of the plaintiffs to have placed a hook on the screen and not the duty of the defendants, owners

new.notes: A tenant (Mrs. Sledge) sub-letting part of a dwelling to another family for rent is treated as an unremarkable, enforceable ordinary lease relationship, governed by standard landlord-tenant repair-duty rules; no explicit duration of the sub-tenancy is stated in the facts, so duration_of_occupancy is left unclear.
Agricultural land lease/provisional-seizure dispute over crop rent; no lodging/dwelling issue.
Farm-lease ejectment dispute over fence/terrace upkeep and appellate jurisdiction; no lodging issue.

A prospective purchaser under a failed agreement of sale took possession of the whole property and owes occupancy rent; this is an ordinary occupancy-pending-sale dispute, not a householder/commercial letting of rooms or a lodging/boarding arrangement.

Automobile-accident tort suit; the mother's rooming house is mentioned only in passing to compute her lost rental income ($5/week per room) as an element of damages, not to adjudicate any lodging issue.

Dispute between a landlord's statutory lien and a prior chattel mortgage on furniture in a building leased for a boarding-house business; addresses lien-priority ranking under the chattel mortgage act, not the legal character or regulation of the boarding-house occupancy itself.

new.holding_summary: An individual landlord who leased four rooms in a dwelling house to a tenant family at $40/month obtained a writ of provisional seizure over the tenant's furniture after the tenant fell behind on rent and began removing property; the court held the tenant's indebtedness and removal of furniture from the leased premises afforded ground for the writ, and affirmed judgment for the landlord.

quotes.text: In February, 1922, defendant, Grady C. Wheeler, leased from plaintiff- four; rooms in á dwelling house • in Shreveport at a monthly rental of $40.00.

The fact that he was indebted to plaintiff for rent and that he removed part of his furniture from the leased premises afforded ground for the writ of provisional seizure.

new.notes: An individual householder-landlord letting rooms in her own dwelling house to a family for monthly rent is treated as an ordinary, fully enforceable lease (rent recoverable, landlord's lien enforceable by provisional seizure), a favorable ordinary-incident-of-ownership pattern.
Possessory action over land and a ginhouse; no lodging issue.
Landlord's liability for a commercial tenant's tortious removal of a third party's advertising sign under C.C. art. 2703; ordinary commercial tenancy, no dwelling/room letting or lodging content.
Landlord's liability for damage to tenant's piano from falling plaster; ordinary repair/maintenance dispute, not a lodging or short-term-occupancy case.
Priority dispute between lessor's privilege and an insurer's premium claim in a corporate receivership; no occupancy or lodging content.
Peddler/hawker license-tax case; a boarding-house keeper (Mrs. Turner) appears only as one of defendant's meat-delivery customers, with no adjudication of her letting arrangement's legal character.
Boundary-line/fence possessory-injunction dispute between adjoining landowners; no letting or lodging content.

Tort suit against a constable and his deputy for illegally ejecting a $5/month household tenant's furniture without the statutory 24-hour warrant; ordinary long-term residential tenancy and eviction-procedure holding, not a lodging/boarding characterization case.
Election contest turning on voters' domicile and residence for voting eligibility; no dwelling-letting or lodging content.
Dispute over whether a landlord's judgment for the full unexpired rent term barred a later suit to cancel the lease; ordinary commercial/residential lease-enforcement doctrine, no lodging content.

Hotel Astor guests and an ejected visitor; the holding turns entirely on plaintiff's violation of the hotel's opposite-sex visiting rule and consequent assault/ejection, not on the legal character of the guests' hotel occupancy, so characterization/holding_summary are left null for lack of a supporting quote (requirement 1).
Damage suit against a commercial storefront tenant for holding over past lease expiration and consequent lost sub-lease; commercial holdover/attorney's-fees dispute, no lodging content.

Building contractor's suit against husband and wife for construction/repairs on the wife's paraphernal property; a construction-debt and marital-property-liability dispute, not a lodging/letting case.
Commercial-floor tenant's trespass claim against landlord's repair contractors, resolved on plaintiff's consent to the entry; no lodging or dwelling-letting content.

Cemetery association vault 'lease' reclassified as a contract of deposit rather than a true lease; the lease-vs-deposit reasoning is analogous to lease-vs-license doctrine but concerns a burial vault, not a dwelling or room.
Rents/trespass dispute between adjoining landowners over a tenant's dairy cows and shed straying onto plaintiff's lot; commercial dairy-tenant lease, no lodging content.
Truck-farm ground lease and dispute over the value of a building erected by the lessee; agricultural lease, not dwelling/room letting.

Married woman's suit to recover rent on a dwelling house leased to a company secretary for a dental-manufacturing venture; testimony mentions the company chemist's family having separately been lodged in a Magazine Street boarding house he rented himself, but that boarding arrangement is background only, not adjudicated.
Prescription of a common alleyway servitude between abutting lot owners; no letting or occupancy-for-pay content.

Damage suit for a credit-seller's illegal entry into plaintiff's home to repossess a piano; plaintiff's household included 'Mrs. Chandler, a boarder or sub-tenant,' but the holding is entirely about the illegality of the repossession, with no adjudication of the boarder arrangement's legal character.

new.cite: Brierre v. Ricehulling Mfg. Co., 6 Teiss. 142
new.notes: Suit over unpaid commercial rent and removal of merchandise under lessor's privilege; no dwelling/lodging issue.
Ordinary year-long lease of an entire residence; dispute is about habitability/repairs and reconvention pleading, not lodging or short-term letting.
Boundary/fence encroachment dispute between adjoining owners; no letting or occupancy issue.
Dispute over landlord's privilege on a leased commercial cigar stand and sale of the 'right of occupancy' of a business lease; not dwelling lodging.
Ownership/partition dispute concerning reimbursement for taxes and improvements; res judicata issue, no letting/lodging.

Ordinary uncontested monthly lease of one half of a double cottage to a tenant; dispute is solely over whether an adjoining yard/lot was included, not over the character or legality of the letting itself.
Dispute over transfer of a paving privilege to sale proceeds in a judicial partition; unrelated to lodging.

new.cite: L'Hote & Co. v. Church Extension Society of the Methodist Episcopal Church, 3 Teiss. 305
new.notes: Service-of-process and mechanic's-lien dispute over a church building occupied by a congregation with the owner's permission; court notes landlord-tenant relation did not exist, but no compensated dwelling occupancy at issue.
Dispute over whether chandeliers were movables passing with a sale of a house; no occupancy/letting issue.
Third-opposition proceeding over priority between landlord's rent privilege and a wage-earner's privilege in a judicial sale; no dwelling/lodging issue.

new.cite: Waldrop v. Singer Sewing Machine Co., 14 Teiss. 384
new.notes: Repossession of a leased sewing machine from plaintiff's home; concerns movable-property lease/sale law, not dwelling occupancy.
Suit over possession of a union membership card (bailment/capacity to sue); unrelated to lodging.
Lease of an unimproved vacant lot of ground, not a dwelling; dispute over tendered rent and termination of the lease.

Party-wall dispute between adjoining owners (destination du pere de famille); no letting/occupancy issue.

Dedication of land as a public cemetery/graveyard; no occupancy-for-pay or lodging issue at all.

new.notes: Dispute over right to lease outer wall advertising space between competing lessees; no dwelling/room occupancy involved.
Nullity of an unappraised sheriff's sale for a paving lien; possession/ratification doctrine, no lodging or boarding issue.
Landlord's lien suit on rent notes for a leased commercial premises and a sale-vs-lease dispute over a slicing machine; not a dwelling/lodging case.
Bare ejectment for nonpayment of rent; opinion is one paragraph and gives no facts on the nature, duration, or type of premises let.

new.cite: Uniola Real Estate Co. v. Levy Lattress Co., 5 Pelt. 183
new.notes: Commercial lease of a building to a mattress manufacturer; dispute over increased fire-insurance premium, not a dwelling/lodging matter.
Dispute over rent/interest owed by an auction adjudicatee pending passage of a sale act during a succession partition; no lodging or dwelling-letting issue.
Injunction suit over enforcement of a jitney/bus transportation ordinance during a streetcar strike; police-power regulation but of street transportation, not lodging or boarding houses.

new.cite: Bisso v. Mayor of Morgan City, 169 La. 122
