new.cite: Parish of Orleans v. Barzana, 3 Pelt. 371
new.holding_summary: The Parish sought to enjoin and abate as a nuisance a house alleged to be used for prostitution or assignation, naming the tenant and the two property owners as defendants. The court found, after extensive testimony, that the premises were in fact operated as a legitimate boarding and rooming house housing respectable, often married, long-term occupants, and not a house of ill fame. The trial court's dismissal of the abatement suit and injunction was affirmed.

new.holding_summary: A judgment awarding the plaintiff the full stated value of chattels seized in an underlying replevin action (never prosecuted by the replevin plaintiff) was reversed because the trial court applied an incorrect measure of damages. The court held that a bare valuation in a replevin affidavit or bond is not conclusive, and here plaintiff's own proof showed a co-defendant, a boardinghouse proprietor, asserted a lien on the chattels for board and lodging furnished. A new trial was ordered to determine plaintiff's actual interest in the chattels against that boardinghouse keeper's lien claim.

the chattels described in the complaint in replevin were brought to the house of the said Cora M. Bice by Samuel J. Budracco, and that the chattels were detained by the defendant Rice under and by virtue of her lien for food and lodging

Where in an action against the surety on an undertaking in replevin to recover possession of certain household chattels it is conceded that the plaintiff in replevin did not prosecute that action, and the sole proof in the present action as to any interest of the plaintiff in the chattels is by the presumption arising from the fact that the marshal in his return states that he took the property from the possession of the defendant in the replevin action, and the plaintiff here introduces proof that one of the defendants claims a boarding-house lien on the chattels, a judgment in favor of the plaintiff for the full value of the chattels will be reversed, on the ground that the court did not apply the proper rule of damages, for if, on a new trial hereby ordered, it appears that plaintiff has no right at all to the possession of the chattels, she will be entitled to nominal damages only.

Liquor-tax certificate revocation over sufficiency of neighboring-dwelling-owner consents and building entrances; consent-counting mechanics, not lodging/boarding regulation or letting.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Street-railway collision personal-injury case; no relation to letting dwellings or lodging regulation. Retrieval mismatch.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Eviction/constructive-eviction dispute between a landlord and the commercial lessee running the Albemarle Hotel, arising from adjoining construction damage. Building setback-line restrictive covenant dispute over a two-family house; no lodging/boarding facts.
Ejectment/adverse-possession dispute among cotenant heirs over title to real property; no lodging/boarding or short-term letting facts.

new.holding_summary: Accounting dispute among tenants in common of inherited real estate over taxes, repairs, and rent-collection commissions; the widow-occupant's use of the homestead is discussed only as an incident of cotenancy, not as a letting to a paying occupant.
new.notes: Tenants-in-common accounting case; no compensated letting of rooms/dwelling to a third party is at issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: A boarding-house keeper sued two sets of guests who had contracted for rooms and board for the June-to-October season but left early and refused to pay. The appellate term held the trial court applied the wrong measure of damages, awarding the full unpaid contract price instead of the plaintiff's lost profits. Damages should be limited to the difference between the contract price and what it would have cost plaintiff to board the defendants had they stayed.

quotes.text: the defendants engaged rooms and board at his hoarding-house for the season from June 1 to October 1, 1907
were brought hy plaintiff to recover damages for breach of a contract for hoard and lodgings
The plaintiff is only entitled to the loss of profits which resulted from the failure of defendants to complete their contract.

new.court: County Court of New York, Albany County
new.holding_summary: Summary proceeding to remove a vendee in possession under an executory land-purchase contract; court holds a vendee is not a squatter/licensee removable under the summary-proceedings statute.
new.notes: Vendor-vendee dispute over land contract, not a lodging/room-letting arrangement despite license-vs-squatter language.

new.holding_summary: Whether a party-wall contribution covenant runs with the land and binds successive grantees; unrelated to occupancy for pay.
new.notes: Party-wall covenant case; no bearing on lodging/boarding.

new.holding_summary: Ultra vires and nuisance analysis of a stage-coach company's exterior advertising signs; municipal ordinance on street advertising upheld. No occupancy of dwellings/rooms involved.
new.notes: Corporate ultra vires / municipal ordinance case about advertising signs, not lodging.

new.holding_summary: Liquor Tax Law cancellation proceeding turning on whether a building used partly as a church and partly as the pastor's dwelling was used 'exclusively' as a church for purposes of the 200-foot distance rule.
new.notes: Liquor-license distance case; the dwelling use discussed is the pastor's own residence, not a paying-occupant letting.

new.holding_summary: Enforcement of a subdivision deed's building-setback restrictive covenant against a defendant building too close to the street line.
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant/setback case; no compensated occupancy issue.

new.holding_summary: Receiver's suit to set aside a corporation's chattel mortgage on hotel furniture as an unauthorized corporate act under the Stock Corporation Law; mortgage upheld as a renewed purchase-money mortgage.
new.notes: Corporate/chattel-mortgage law case; the 'apartment hotel' operated by the mortgagor tenant is mentioned only in passing background facts.

new.holding_summary: Contract dispute over an exclusive taxicab-stand concession at a hotel entrance, held invalid as contrary to a municipal ordinance restricting hotel cab stands to hotel guests.
new.notes: Cab-stand concession case; hotel guests mentioned only as the class of persons the cabs may serve, not an issue of room letting.

new.court: County Court of New York, Otsego County
new.holding_summary: Peddling-ordinance case invalidating a municipal ordinance that discriminated between vendors using horse-drawn versus hand-drawn carts; unrelated to housing or lodging.
new.notes: Street-peddling ordinance case; no lodging/boarding content.

new.holding_summary: Demurrer sustained in a penalty action against a boarding-house keeper for failing to post 'Oleomargarine Used Here' signs, because the complaint failed to allege the oleomargarine was served as a butter substitute.
new.notes: Food-labeling regulation applied incidentally to a boarding house among hotels/restaurants/saloons generally; the pleading defect decided is unrelated to the legality or character of letting/lodging itself.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: Summary dispossess proceeding against a chattel mortgagee of saloon fixtures/lease; mortgagee not liable for rent absent actual occupation or control of the premises.
new.notes: Commercial saloon lease/chattel-mortgage assignment case; not about lodging/dwelling occupancy.

new.court: County Court of New York, Oneida County
new.holding_summary: Partition action; widow occupying the homestead with her infant son as guardian in socage held not accountable to cotenants for rental value absent an agreement to pay rent or proof of ouster.
new.notes: Cotenancy/partition accounting case; testimony that other persons 'more or less' occupied the premises with the widow does not establish a paying letting.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: A landlord sued her former tenant for damage done to furniture in a furnished apartment let for eight months. Both sides tried the case, without objection, on the theory that the measure of damages was the cost of repairs, and that theory became the law of the case. The appellate term limited the landlord's recovery accordingly, ordering a new trial unless plaintiff stipulated to reduce the judgment to the proven repair cost.

quotes.text: The defendant rented furnished apartments from the plaintiff and occupied them for a period of eight months.
The defendant rented furnished apartments from the plaintiff and occupied them for a period of eight months.

Where the trial of an action against a tenant of a furnished apartment for damages to the furniture proceeded upon the theory that the test of the measure of damages was the cost of repairs to the furniture, judgment in favor of the landlord must be so limited in amount.

new.notes: who_was_letting left unclear: opinion does not indicate whether plaintiff let a single furnished apartment as a householder or operated multiple furnished apartments as a business.

new.holding_summary: Will construction: language directing a legatee to pay over shares of business profits construed as a covenant rather than a void perpetual trust.
new.notes: Testamentary trust/covenant construction case unrelated to lodging.

new.holding_summary: Commercial store lease; whether municipal removal of an encroaching stoop and reconfiguration of the store entrance constituted a partial eviction excusing rent. Held no eviction; rent due in full.
new.notes: Commercial shop-front lease dispute, not a dwelling/lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Contract to erect an advertising sign on the exterior wall of a building held to create a license, not a lease, because it conveyed no estate or possessory interest in the realty; injunction against interference denied for other reasons.
new.notes: Applies license-vs-lease doctrine to a wall-advertising contract, not to occupancy of a dwelling/rooms by a person; no compensated occupancy of the premises is at issue, so marked irrelevant despite doctrinal overlap.

new.holding_summary: School-tuition dispute over whether a family that rented rooms in another district for the school year was 'residing' there for purposes of free public schooling; held yes, resident though not domiciled there.
new.notes: The family's renting of rooms is background fact only; the holding concerns residence vs. domicile for school-district purposes, not the legal character or regulation of the letting itself. Opinion in dicta cites Stacom v. Moon (a landlady leasing a house to keep a seasonal boarding house, May-October) but that is not this case's holding.
Dispute over water-meter rates for an apartment house's café/bar/garage under the city charter; no bearing on letting rooms/dwellings or its regulation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Election-of-remedies dispute between landlord and long-term tenant (ejectment vs. summary nonpayment proceeding); no lodging/short-term letting issue.

new.cite: Harbor & Suburban Building & Savings Ass'n v. Employers' Liability Assurance Corp., 79 Misc. 150
new.notes: Liability-insurance coverage dispute over roof repairs and a warranty that premises were 'occupied as Apartment Hotel'; the apartment-hotel label is only an insurance term, not a ruling on letting/lodging practice.
Partition action; receiver of rents seeks instructions on collecting rent/use-and-occupation from a co-tenant with dower rights occupying the family home. No compensated lodger/boarder arrangement.
Enforcement of a deed covenant restricting lots to residential-only buildings against construction of a business block; no letting or lodging of rooms at issue.

new.court: County Court of New York, Oneida County
new.notes: Dispute over validity of a lease-renewal endorsement following a trust-deed conveyance of the fee; ordinary commercial lease/trust title question, not lodging or short-term letting.

new.notes: Domicile determination for transfer-tax purposes; decedent's apartment in a hotel is mentioned only as evidence of a New York 'home,' not as a ruling on letting/lodging law.
Mandamus to compel issuance of a moving-picture-show license under Buffalo's zoning/licensing ordinance; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

Occupancy was incident to a master-servant employment contract, not a paid lodger/tenant arrangement; addresses when service-occupancy terminates for summary removal, a distinct doctrine from compensated short-term letting.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Ordinary $12/month apartment tenancy; dispute is whether tenant could set off a bank deposit against rent following the landlord's bank failure/bankruptcy, turning on classification of the tenancy as monthly. No lodging-house or short-let characterization issue.

new.cite: People ex rel. Lankton v. Roberts, 90 Misc. 439
new.notes: Mandamus challenge to a municipal residence-district ordinance under the Housing Act barring an undertaking business; concerns land-use zoning power, not letting of rooms/dwellings for pay.
Breach-of-covenant-for-quiet-enjoyment action arising from a 21-year commercial ground lease and prior vexatious ejectment/dispossess suits; not a lodging/short-term letting case.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Landlord leased an entire hotel building to a tenant to operate the hotel/saloon business; dispute concerns a side-door easement and partial eviction, not the legal character of guest occupancy or its regulation.
Conditional-sale-of-furniture dispute under the Personal Property Law; plaintiff's employment 'running a rooming-house' is mentioned only in passing as background, not adjudicated.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Rent-arrears action turning on whether a mortgage-foreclosure holdover tenancy was monthly or an indefinite hiring under Real Property Law §232; ordinary commercial tenancy, not lodging.
Dispute over an oil-drilling lease/option and ownership of oil wells; unrelated to dwelling/room letting.

new.cite: In re the Estate of Kane, 93 Misc. 406
new.notes: Domicile determination for an invalid decedent temporarily residing away from his furnished Newport residence; no letting/lodging issue presented.

new.cite: Syracuse Malleable Iron Works v. Travelers' Insurance, 94 Misc. 411
new.notes: Employer's liability insurance coverage dispute over roof-repair work after a fire; 'apartment hotel' appears only in the facts of a cited precedent (Harbor & S.B. & S. Assn.), not this case's own facts.

new.court: County Court of New York, Niagara County
new.notes: Commercial lease of manufacturing premises (Flaxen Fibre-Down Company) and holdover tenancy; not lodging/boarding of individuals.

new.cite: People ex rel. Doyle v. Atwell, 232 N.Y. 96
new.notes: Municipal ordinance requiring a mayoral permit for public street meetings; habeas corpus and free-speech case, unconnected to letting of dwellings.
Landlord's duty to maintain a common back yard for tenants' child injured therein; concerns premises-liability for common areas, not the letting/lodging arrangement itself.
Restrictive covenant limiting building to a 'first-class private dwelling' for one family, enforced against use as a music school; not about paid lodging or boarders.
Restrictive covenant dispute over converting a single-family house into a two-family apartment; concerns structural/use covenants, not paid lodging.

Case concerns a private residential park association's rules restricting street access for guests; 'established and recognized boarding houses and inns' are mentioned only in passing as exempt from a guest-count rule, not as the subject of adjudication.
Alien Property Custodian's authority to seize and sell real property of an enemy alien; unrelated to lodging or letting practice.

quotes.text: In April, 1926, Cornelius Byrne leased a house to be used as a boarding house at Long Beach to Mrs. Padden for the summer season.

With afiiairs in this condition an accord was reached. In return for her continuance as tenant and paying $500, Mr. Byrne was to permit her to remain for the rest of the season and release his claim for $1,200. And there was a satisfaction for he not only accepted the check but had it certified.

new.notes: The case does not describe the individual boarders' occupancy; 'duration_of_occupancy' reflects the seasonal (summer) term of Padden's own leasehold under which she was to operate the boarding house.
Dispute over validity of delivery of a deed held in escrow; unrelated to lodging or letting.
Restrictive covenant confining use to a private residence for one family, enforced against use as a maternity hospital; not about paid lodging or boarders.
Specific performance/marketable title dispute involving restrictive covenants and party-wall agreements; no connection to lodging or letting of rooms.

Plaintiffs boarded and cared for an elderly homeowner in exchange for an oral promise to devise his house to them; this is a personal caregiving/inheritance arrangement decided under the Statute of Frauds and part-performance doctrine, not a commercial letting or lodging transaction.
Dispute over exclusive hunting/fishing leases in navigable waters of Great South Bay; unrelated to lodging.

new.cite: Stern v. Equitable Trust Co., 238 N.Y. 267
new.notes: Concerns a hold-over apartment tenant's liability for rent under the Emergency Rent Laws after expiration of a definite-term lease; ordinary apartment tenancy/rent-regulation dispute, not about short-term room letting or boarding-house lodging.

new.cite: In re the Accounting of O'Donnell, 240 N.Y. 99
new.notes: Breach-of-covenant-of-quiet-enjoyment claim arising from a commercial lease (grain company) that lapsed on the life tenant's death; not related to lodging or room letting.

new.cite: Dalton v. Hamilton Hotel Operating Co., 242 N.Y. 481
new.notes: Plaintiff had leased an apartment (year-long term) at an apartment hotel; the holding concerns the hotel's gratuitous-bailment liability for lost trunks, not the legal character or regulation of the letting/lodging arrangement.

new.cite: People ex rel. Fordham Manor Reformed Church v. Walsh, 244 N.Y. 280
new.notes: Zoning variance dispute over permitting a garage in a residence district; unrelated to lodging or letting of rooms.

new.notes: Zoning variance dispute over a garage permit; no bearing on letting or lodging.

new.holding_summary: Pleading case on whether conducting a real estate and insurance business from part of a dwelling violates a restrictive covenant limiting use to a private dwelling; judgment on the pleadings was improper in a doubtful case.
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute about a home office/business use, not about letting rooms or lodgers.

new.holding_summary: Vendor-purchaser dispute over whether an undisclosed restrictive covenant against liquor sales rendered title unmarketable; reformation of the contract was denied.
new.notes: Title/incumbrance dispute concerning a liquor-sale covenant; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting.

new.cite: Klepper v. Seymour House Corp. of Ogdensburg, Inc., 246 N.Y. 85

new.notes: Negligence/nuisance case about a hotel building's maintenance duty toward the street; the leasing of stores under the hotel is background only, not a dispute over letting rooms.

new.holding_summary: Constitutional challenge to the Multiple Dwelling Law under the Home Rule Amendment; the court held the law a valid State health measure not restricted to local 'property, affairs or government of cities.'
new.notes: Pure Home Rule/constitutional-classification dispute over tenement-house regulation; the opinions do not discuss lodgers, boarders, or short-term letting practices.

new.holding_summary: Declaratory-judgment action over whether a common grantor was bound to impose a uniform half-acre (or one-acre) minimum-lot-size restriction on unsold parcels of a residential subdivision; no such reciprocal restriction was implied absent disclosure to the buyers.
new.notes: The deed covenants list 'boarding house' among prohibited uses, but the actual controversy is minimum subdivision-lot acreage; boarding-house use is never litigated.

new.cite: Millhiser v. Beau Site Co., 251 N.Y. 290
new.holding_summary: Construing General Business Law section 200, the court held a hotel's $250 statutory limit on liability for guests' safe-deposited valuables applies even where the loss is caused by theft by the hotel's own employee, but the hotel could not invoke the limitation because it failed to post the statute itself alongside its safe-deposit notice.
new.notes: Concerns an innkeeper's statutory liability limit for guests' valuables, not the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging arrangements.

new.holding_summary: Dog-bite action turning on whether Gramercy Park, a privately controlled square, was a 'public place' under the Sanitary Code's anti-muzzling ordinance; held it was not, so the ordinance did not apply.
new.notes: Definition of 'public place' for a dog ordinance; unrelated to letting or lodging.

new.cite: Varriale v. Brooklyn Edison Co., 252 N.Y. 222

new.notes: Party-wall/easement dispute over an advertising sign; unrelated to lodging or letting.

new.cite: Gray v. Kaufman Dairy & Ice Cream Co., 162 N.Y. 388

new.notes: Commercial storefront lease/surrender dispute; unrelated to residential lodging or boarding.

new.holding_summary: A tenant in common in possession of land who quarried and sold rock without cotenant consent must account to the cotenants for the value of the rock taken, as waste diminishing the common estate.
new.notes: Tenancy-in-common/waste accounting dispute over quarried rock; no connection to letting or lodging.

new.cite: Donnelly v. City of Rochester, 166 N.Y. 315
new.holding_summary: Wrongful-death action against a city for an inadequately guarded areaway on a sidewalk; the sufficiency of the guard rail was a jury question, and the city was chargeable with notice of the long-standing danger.
new.notes: Municipal sidewalk-negligence case; unrelated to lodging or letting.

new.cite: People ex rel. Pumpyansky v. Keating, 168 N.Y. 390

new.notes: Street-encroachment licensing dispute over news stands; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.cite: Cudlip v. New York Evening Journal Publishing Co., 174 N.Y. 158
new.holding_summary: Libel action reversed for improper admission of an ex parte affidavit exonerating the plaintiff of a theft charge; the affidavit's prejudicial effect on damages required a new trial.
new.notes: A boarding house (kept by a Mrs. Morgan, where the plaintiff had boarded) is mentioned only in passing as background to a libel/evidence dispute over a stolen ring; not relevant under the passing-mention exclusion.

new.cite: People ex rel. Lieberman v. Vandecarr, 175 N.Y. 440
new.holding_summary: Habeas corpus challenge to a Sanitary Code section requiring a Board of Health permit to sell milk; the permit requirement was upheld as a reasonable exercise of the police power.
new.notes: Public-health licensing case about milk sales; unrelated to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: Upheld, as a valid police-power health measure, the Labor Law provision limiting bakery employees to sixty hours per week / ten hours per day.
new.notes: Bakery labor-hours regulation case; unrelated to lodging or short-term letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: A three-story building interiorly divided so each floor could house a separate family violated a restrictive covenant against tenement houses and requiring private dwellings only; the remedy was an injunction against tenement-house use rather than demolition.
new.notes: Concerns a private covenant against permanent multi-family (tenement) division of a residence, not compensated short-term letting of rooms to lodgers or boarders.
Nuisance/damages case re: soot and vibration from an electric plant fouling a hotel; measure-of-damages dispute, not about the legal character or regulation of letting rooms.
Civil rights statute case holding a bootblacking stand is not a 'place of public accommodation'; no bearing on lodging/letting rooms despite listing inns/hotels in the statute's enumeration.
Contract/assignment and patent-damages dispute over printing presses and a restraint-of-trade covenant; 'lease' language refers to leasing presses to purchasers, unrelated to dwelling occupancy.

Home-rule constitutional challenge to the office of state superintendent of elections; mentions power to inspect hotels/lodging-houses and require lodger registers as an investigative tool only, not a case about the legal character of letting rooms.
Boundary/title dispute between tenants in common re: a beach plot and bathhouse; not about compensated occupancy of dwellings/rooms.
Cattle-trespass liability case discussing fencing statutes and 'incident of ownership' of land; unrelated to letting dwellings/rooms.

Statutory-repeal case distinguishing 'apartment house' from 'tenement house' under NYC Building Code vs. Tenement House Act, based on physical amenities (kitchen, bathtub, water closet per family); a large multi-family building is at issue, but the holding is purely about which regulatory code applies, not about the legality/character of letting rooms or lodger status.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute over a synagogue building addition ('one house' restriction); the restriction applies to dwelling houses vs. churches, not to letting of rooms for compensation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Eminent-domain interest-on-award dispute in a street-widening proceeding; unrelated to lodging/letting law.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Short per curiam on ejectment/possession under a lease of town land (Willetts lease); no facts about dwelling rooms or lodgers.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: Plaintiffs bought a lease of premises operated as a rooming house, along with the furniture, but a provision of the underlying lease restricted use of the premises 'solely as a private dwelling,' preventing them from taking roomers; the court held a temporary injunction against enforcement of the purchase-money notes and chattel mortgage was improperly granted because plaintiffs neither tendered back the property nor sought rescission, and had an adequate remedy at law.

quotes.text: The plaintiffs bought of the defendants a lease of premises containing a rooming house and the business therein conducted, and the furniture therein, and claim that it was represented that the house could be used for the purpose of a rooming house and that the furniture therein was the defendant-seller’s property.

They allege that the furniture was not defendants’ property and thereafter was removed, and that they cannot use the house for roomers by reason of a provision of the lease that it may be used solely as a private dwelling.

new.notes: Case recites (but does not itself adjudicate the merits of) a lease clause confining the premises to 'private dwelling' use and excluding rooming-house operation, an adverse-leaning fact pattern; the court's actual holding is on equity procedure (rescission/tender), so characterization is left null since the court did not itself classify the arrangement.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Partition suit involving curtesy tenancy and burden of proof on live birth of a child; no bearing on letting of dwellings/rooms.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Conversion action over trade fixtures (a portable concession building) at an amusement park under a weekly catering-privilege tenancy; not about occupancy of dwelling rooms.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Telephone-conduit-in-street easement/servitude case re: abutting fee owners; unrelated to lodging or letting of rooms.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Bailment dispute over trunks lost by an apartment hotel that stored them for a tenant pending occupancy; the apartment-hotel lease (private-dwelling use) is incidental background, and the holding turns entirely on gratuitous-bailee liability, not on the character or regulation of letting rooms.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Farm-on-shares lease/eviction and summary-proceedings res judicata dispute; unrelated to letting of dwelling rooms.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Partition of a joint bank account between divorced spouses; unrelated to lodging/letting law.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Prosecution for running a tailoring business in the defendant's own tenement apartment in violation of the Building Zone Resolution; reversed on ultra vires/notice grounds. Concerns a resident's own commercial use of his apartment, not letting rooms to others for pay.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department
new.holding_summary: Marriage-annulment jurisdiction case holding that substituted service by publication did not confer jurisdiction over a non-resident defendant.
new.notes: Domicile facts note the couple 'occupying furnished rooms at several different addresses'; purely incidental to jurisdiction/domicile analysis, not a letting or boarding dispute.

new.cite: Couch v. Farmers' Fire Insurance of York, 64 A.D. 367
new.holding_summary: Fire insurance policy voided under a 'vacant or unoccupied' clause where the insured left her dwelling unattended for nearly five months.
new.notes: Retrieved passage discusses an owner's residual 'interest in protection and preservation' of a vacant house for insurance-occupancy purposes; unrelated to compensated letting or lodging.

new.cite: Safee v. City of Buffalo, 204 A.D. 561

new.holding_summary: Sustained under the police power a Buffalo ordinance licensing and regulating the sale of soft drinks in the wake of Prohibition-era enforcement problems.
new.notes: Police-power licensing case about soda/soft-drink retailers, not lodging or boarding houses; selector matched on generic 'regulation'/police-power language.

new.cite: McLean v. F. W. Woolworth Co., 204 A.D. 118
new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
new.holding_summary: Held that a one-story-height restriction in an 1881 deed was a personal covenant benefiting only the grantor, not a covenant running with the land binding a later-erected building.
new.notes: Quoted 'nuisance'/occupancy language is from a different case (Clark v. Devoe) cited for covenant-construction principles; the dispute itself concerns building-height restrictions, not lodging or paying occupants.

new.cite: People ex rel. Van Norder v. Sewer, Water & Street Commission, 90 A.D. 555
new.holding_summary: Upheld revocation of a hackman's license for soliciting patronage on public streets in violation of statute and license conditions.
new.notes: Police-power licensing case about cab/hackman regulation on public streets; no connection to lodging or boarding houses despite selector match on 'regulation' language.

new.holding_summary: Murder conviction reversed for exclusion of physical evidence and erroneous jury instructions on flight and good-character evidence.

new.cite: In re the Transfer Tax on Estate Conveyed in Trust for His Own Benefit of Craig, 97 A.D. 289

new.holding_summary: The court held that a boarding-house keeper could not hold a married woman personally liable for her family's board bill absent an express agreement to pay, because the common-law duty to support the family -- and hence liability for necessaries such as board and lodging -- rests presumptively on the husband; the wife's trunks retained under the keeper's claimed lien were ordered released.

quotes.text: furnished to the plaintiff and to Jacob Buhl, her husband, at the request of the plaintiff and her said husband, accommodation, board and lodging

The plaintiff brings this action to recover certain trunks containing her personal wardrobe, or- their value, such trunks being retained by the defendant, a boarding-house keeper, who claims a lien upon the same for the amount of a board bill aggregating something over $150.
liability for necessaries, furnished to the family of a married man is presumptively and primarily upon the husband, unless the wife by express agreement charges herself personally with the same

new.notes: Occupancy ran roughly May-July 1903 (about two months) before the family departed; treated as ordinary/months rather than unclear given the stated dates.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, First Department

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
new.holding_summary: A conditional vendor of a piano who failed to file or deliver a duplicate of his conditional sale contract as required by the 1897 Lien Law could not defeat the claim of a boarding-house keeper who, as a good-faith pledgee, had acquired a statutory lien on the piano left with her by a boarder for an unpaid board bill.

quotes.text: Arthur J. Mann, Mrs. Mann, his wife, and their son became boarders at the boarding house of Mrs. Jane Davis in Albany and he brought with him the piano and furniture for his rooms.
Mrs. Davis, under section 71 of the Lien Law (Laws of 1897, chap. 418), acquired a lien upon the piano for the hoard which she was furnishing from day to day to Mrs. Mann, her husband and son.
I think the evidence clearly shows that Mrs. Davis was a pledgee .in good faith of the piano.

new.holding_summary: A son-in-law who received his mother-in-law into the home he shared with his wife could not recover from her estate for board and lodging furnished, absent proof of an express contract to pay. The court held that the law does not imply an obligation to pay for board and lodging furnished by a relative who takes in a family member, and any parol contract must be shown by disinterested or corroborating testimony. The claimant's proof, resting mainly on his own and his wife's testimony, was held insufficient.

quotes.text: The theory of the claimant, however, is that the intestate agreed to pay a weekly sum for her board and lodging.
The law should not imply an obligation to pay, inasmuch as the claimant is a son-in-law of the intestate and received her into the home occupied by him and his wife.

In order to entitle a son-in-law to recover from the estate of his mother-in-law moneys alleged to be due for board and lodging furnished to the decedent, a contract to pay therefor must be established, either by written evidence, or, if established by parol, it must be by the testimony of disinterested witnesses, or the contract must be corroborated by them in all substantial particulars.

new.notes: Family-lodging context (son-in-law/mother-in-law) rather than the stranger-lodger scenario at the core of the project's inquiry; coded mixed/lodging because the court treats board-for-pay as legally cognizable but declines to imply it within a household-family relationship absent proof; duration left unclear because the opinion describes an extended, unspecified multi-year stay rather than a discrete nights/weeks/months period.

new.holding_summary: A married woman who, under agreement with her husband that she alone would receive the compensation, took a boarder into their household for pay covering room, board, and care, may sue and recover for that board and rent in her own name; the arrangement is treated as an ordinary lawful household boarding business, with the wife's right to contract for her own earnings enforced notwithstanding the common-law rule that a husband otherwise owns the proceeds of boarders taken into his house.

quotes.text: Where a husband, as the head of the household, takes boarders into his house, and his wife takes charge of the house, and thus aids the husband in carrying on the business so maintained in the house, her services and earnings belong to the husband, notwithstanding the statutes of recent years in regard to married women and their separate estates.

Where a married couple take a boarder into their home under an agreement between the wife and her husband that she alone shall receive the compensation therefor, the common-law rights of the husband are abrogated, and the wife may recover for the board in her own name.

The right of a married woman to contract with her husband enables her, however, to enter into an agreement with him by which she is to receive the compensation for her personal services in the care and attention given to persons within the household, and she may also enter into an agreement with him by which she is to have the gross proceeds of the business so to be conducted even in his house, and his agreement therefore is binding upon him.

new.notes: Sunday-closing-law/theater-licensing case concerning moving-picture shows; unrelated to lodging or dwelling occupancy.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: Plaintiff, who kept rooms and let them to lodgers and boarders, agreed to sell her household furniture and the unexpired term of her apartment lease to the defendant for $1,000 so the defendant could take over the rooming business, but the defendant repudiated after plaintiff had prepared to vacate. The court held it was error to direct a verdict for only the plaintiff's van/labor expenses and to withhold her other claimed damage items from the jury.

quotes.text: The plaintiff rented rooms. The defendant was to do the like, and said that, as she had arranged for her own lodgers and boarders, she desired that the plaintiff empty the rooms; promising to make good the loss on taking possession.

Through a broker, the defendant on August SI, 1904, agreed to buy from the plaintiff certain household furniture and the unexpired term of a lease of the premises 160 West Forty-Sixth street for $1,000, payable $200 down, and the balance, $800, on September 15th, when possession was to be given.

new.notes: Court does not itself classify the tenant/lodger arrangement (lease/license/lodging/innkeeping); the dispute is contract damages for the sale of a going lodging/boarding business, so characterization is left null. Relevance rests on the running of a lodgers-and-boarders operation being treated as an ordinary, salable enterprise whose breach the court enforces.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Real-estate broker's commission suit over procuring a tenant; the type of premises/tenant is unaddressed and the case turns on insufficiency of proof of a meeting of minds, not on the character of any letting.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: In an action for unpaid rent under a one-year lease of a furnished house, the tenant defended on the ground she was induced to sign by the landlord's false representations about the heating system and concealment of a defective cesspool, and vacated after about three weeks on her physician's advice. The court held that although New York implies no covenant to repair or warranty of tenantability in an ordinary letting, that rule does not shield a landlord's fraudulent misrepresentation or concealment, and that letting a house furnished and ready for occupancy is a circumstance bearing on that question.

quotes.text: This action is brought to recover the fourth installment of rent pursuant to the terms of a written lease whereby the plaintiff leased a furnished house to the defendant for the term of one year.

I think there is a distinction between the letting of an unfurnished house and one furnished ready for occupancy, and that, where misrepresentation and deceit are claimed, the fact that the house is being let furnished ready for occupancy is a circumstance to be weighed in determining the question of fact.
The defendant went into possession on the 16th of April 1908, and moved out on the 9th of May.

new.notes: Relevance is adjacent rather than central: the case is a fraud/misrepresentation dispute between landlord and tenant, not a challenge to the legality of letting or a lodging-house regulation, but it does treat the furnished letting as an ordinary, enforceable transaction and marks out furnished-letting as a distinct doctrinal category from bare unfurnished leases.
Dispute over deskroom sublet by attorneys in a law office; court's analogy to a boarding/lodging-house roomer's lack of estate is passing dictum, not a holding about letting a dwelling.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Corporate stock-injunction contempt dispute; no occupancy, lodging, or dwelling-letting issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Farm cropping-shares lease and cattle-trespass liability; landlord-tenant of farmland, not a dwelling/lodging arrangement.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant enforcement case barring flats/multi-family construction and setting marketable-title rules; not about compensated room-letting or boarders.
Mandamus to compel the city to operate ferry franchises; no occupancy or lodging issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Street-railway transfer-fare statute construction and lease-of-road corporate law; no occupancy or lodging issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Libel action over master-servant discharge of a racing-stable exercise boy; no occupancy/lodging issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Commercial garage sublease, accrued rent, and surety-discharge dispute arising from summary dispossession; premises are a garage/automobile business, not a dwelling.
Replevin dispute over ownership of an employee's manuscript work product; no occupancy or lodging issue.
Widow and infant heir occupy inherited house together as cotenants/guardian in socage; family co-occupancy accounting dispute, no third-party paying lodger.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Deed-set-aside/duress action; that defendant Terry 'kept a boarding house' and plaintiff had boarded there is background establishing the parties' relationship only, with no holding on lodging/boarding law.
Landlord-tenant dispute over return of a security deposit after summary dispossession; premises/dwelling character not at issue.

new.court: New York County Court, Kings County
new.notes: Criminal official-oppression prosecution of police occupying a cigar store; no lodging/boarding issue, though it does discuss police-power limits generally.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Divorce/adultery evidentiary appeal; a witness's description of himself as 'manager of a furnished room house' is a passing biographical detail with no bearing on lodging law.
Police-power/traffic-ordinance prosecution of a fire department officer for driving on the wrong side of the road; no lodging/boarding issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: The court held that boarding house keepers have a valid lien on a boarder's trunk for unpaid board, defeated only if the amount due is tendered, and reversed a judgment that ordered the trunk released while entering judgment for the boarding house keepers without resolving the disputed tender.

quotes.text: Boarding house keepers have a valid lien on a boarder's trunk, unless the amount due for board is tendered.
If she tendered this amount, the defendants are liable for conversion; if she did' not tender it, the defendants had a valid lien up to the amount due them for board furnished.
The learned trial justice ordered the defendants to give up the trunk, and then gave judgment in their favor.

new.notes: Court treats a boarding house keeper's lien on a boarder's property as an established, enforceable commercial right analogous to an innkeeper's lien.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Hotel-guest baggage bailment dispute governing when the innkeeper-guest relationship terminates; concerns bailment standard of care after checkout, not the letting arrangement's legal character.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Commercial loft partial-eviction dispute over ingress/egress access; not a dwelling/lodging matter.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Dispute between husband and wife over receivership/possession of a leased hotel business against the landlord; no issue of letting rooms or boarding/lodging regulation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Commercial lease of manufacturing floor space; landlord's repair entry held not an eviction. No lodging/boarding issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Purely procedural landlord-tenant dispute over pleading a breach-of-repair-covenant as defense vs. counterclaim in a summary possession action. No lodging/boarding content.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Civil-rights case on whether a bootblack stand is a 'place of public accommodation' under 1895 anti-discrimination statute; unrelated to letting dwellings or boarding-house regulation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Wife (a longtime boarding-house keeper) sues husband's estate for board furnished to him. Boarding-house keeping is background fact only; the holding concerns sufficiency of proof of an implied reimbursement obligation between spouses, not the legal character or regulation of letting/boarding.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Procedural sufficiency of a dispossess petition brought by an executor's agent, and tenant estoppel to deny landlord's title. No lodging/boarding content.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Replevin dispute over a saloon tenant's trade fixtures (urinals, partition, awning) after chattel-mortgage foreclosure. No lodging/boarding issue.

Demurrer in an easement-abandonment action; defendant built an apartment hotel where private stables once stood, but that fact is incidental to the easement pleading question, not the letting practice.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Deed-covenant construction case (does 'tenement house' restriction bar a modern apartment house). Discusses that hotels/boarding houses were common and unrestricted uses in 1873, but the holding turns on covenant interpretation of building type, not on the legal character or regulation of paying-occupant arrangements themselves.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Vendor-purchaser incumbrance dispute over a restrictive covenant against noxious trades; a cited precedent lists 'tenement house, brewery, lager beer saloon' among prohibited uses, but this case itself does not address letting or boarding-house regulation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Libel action over a newspaper's claim that plaintiffs' commercial hotel 'has a bad reputation'; holding concerns pleading of special damages in a property libel, not the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Upholds application of the 1901 Tenement House Act (police-power regulation) against a builder whose construction was not yet under way when the act took effect. Tenement houses here are permanent multi-family apartment buildings, not short-term lodging/boarding houses, and no occupancy or compensated-occupancy issue is presented (dispute is purely about timing of a construction permit); outside the corpus's boarding/lodging-house regulation focus.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Sets the duration of an innkeeper's liability for a departed guest's baggage; a tort/bailment-duty question collateral to the hotel relationship, not a holding on the legality or regulation of letting/lodging arrangements.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Conversion action by an evicted hotel-operator tenant against the landlord over hotel supplies left behind after dispossession. Landlord-tenant/personal-property dispute, not about letting or regulating lodging.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Party-wall agreement dispute between adjoining lot owners; no lodging/boarding content.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Murder prosecution arising from a fight between rival sailors'-boarding-house 'runners.' Boarding houses appear only as the parties' employers/context; the holding concerns jury instructions on self-defense evidence and character evidence, not the legal character or regulation of boarding houses.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Statutory default lease-term rule (Real Prop. Law §202) applied to an oral hiring of commercial premises for a business. No lodging/boarding issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Whether a conventional landlord-tenant relationship arose by implication over a saloon lease assignment, based on rent-payment conduct. No lodging/boarding issue.
Sky-sign/eminent-domain police-power case (advertising structure ordinance); no bearing on letting of dwellings or lodging/boarding regulation.
Fire-insurance forfeiture case turning on vacancy/occupancy of owner's own dwelling; not about compensated letting to lodgers/boarders.
Covenant-running-with-the-land / light-and-air easement dispute; mentions the building was later used 'as a hotel' only incidentally to the covenant analysis, not addressing letting practice.
Innkeeper tort/slander liability for an employee's insult to a hotel guest; addresses scope of innkeeper's implied contract of protection, not the legal character or regulation of letting rooms.
Sidewalk-grating personal-injury case; the matched text ('let rooms, and did repairs') is a passing description of a building manager's duties, not a holding about letting practice.

Landlord premises-liability case construing the statutory definition of 'tenement house' (three families with common right to halls/stairs/yard) for purposes of the hallway-lighting statute; concerns ordinary multi-family tenancy, not compensated short-term letting or boarding/lodging characterization.

Police-power case sustaining sanitary/plumbing requirements (removal of school sinks) in a multi-family tenement house; regulates building sanitation generally, not the letting of rooms/dwellings for pay or licensing of lodging/boarding houses specifically.
Garbage-transportation licensing ordinance struck down as an invalid delegation of arbitrary permit power; no relation to letting or lodging of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: A landlord sought summary dispossession of a tenant who leased premises to be used as a boarding house, on the theory that the premises were being run as a disorderly house. The court found the police officers' testimony (women reading in ordinary dress, no evidence of immoral conduct observed on the premises) insufficient to establish an unlawful use, and reversed the order removing the tenant.

quotes.text: The tenant herein was a lessee of premises ; the lease providing that it should be used and occupied as a boarding house, and for no other purpose.

The evidence fails to show that the defendant kept a house prohibited by law. The mere fact that an immoral woman lives in a house, or visits one, is not sufficient to show that the tenant keeps a bawdy house.
The granting of the order herein was clearly against the weight of evidence, and must be reversed.

new.holding_summary: Plaintiff's assignor, at the request of the defendant's testator, leased a summer cottage and agreed to furnish the testator and his family with board, service, and general care at $100 per week for a five-month period (June 1 to November 1, 1900). After the testator died mid-term and his family moved out, the court held it was a fair jury question whether the parties intended the boarding arrangement to bind the family for the whole five-month period, reversing for a new trial (though also on an evidentiary error).

quotes.text: by which it was agreed that the latter was to pay $ioo per week for the exclusive possession and use of said Beatty Cottage, and stables and premises, for the said period from June 1st to November 1st, 1900, upon condition that the plaintiff's assignor would provide the service and board and have the general care of the said premises during the said period.

I think it was a fair question for the jury, from the circumstances proved by the plaintiff, whether there was an obligation to occupy the premises under the agreement, and that such occupation was to be for the whole period, from the ist of June to the ist of November.

It could not be assumed to have been within the contemplation of the parties that where a person had thus, at the Instigation of another, leased a house for a particular period, with the understanding that the whole house should be reserved for the suse of the party at whose instigation it was leased, such party could terminate the contract at any time

new.notes: Ejectment case about mortgagee-in-possession rights following a life tenant's lease; concerns title/possession priority among mortgagee, reversioner, and lessee, not the character or regulation of lodging/boarding arrangements.
Bakery labor-hours statute (Lochner-line) sustained as police-power regulation of employment; no relation to letting of dwellings or lodging-house regulation.

Summary-proceeding case holding that an informal family arrangement (mother's house owner; daughter and son-in-law to live there, board the mother, and keep the house in repair 'during her pleasure') did not create a landlord-tenant relationship for eviction purposes. This is a family support arrangement without rent or a stranger-lodger, not a compensated letting or boarding-house transaction; not counted as bearing on the corpus's core practice, though doctrinally adjacent to license/tenancy line-drawing.
Municipal sidewalk-encroachment nuisance case (bank building columns); no relation to letting or lodging.

Dispute over return of an earnest-money deposit for the sale of the 'contents and good will of a furnished room house' business; the holding concerns escrow/conversion proof, not the legal character or regulation of letting furnished rooms.
Ordinary commercial lease holding-over case (subtenant's involuntary holdover binds original tenant for another term); no lodging/boarding subject matter.
Saloon lease holding-over/chattel-mortgage dispute; no relation to dwelling letting or lodging.
Commercial lease-renewal option dispute (meat-packing business premises); no lodging/boarding subject matter.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Special Term, Kings County
new.notes: Liquor tax license consent-counting dispute; concerns whether unfinished houses count as 'dwellings' for consent purposes, not compensated occupancy or lodging.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Theater lease dispute over landlord's duty to repair a roof; mentions a nearby hotel only as a locational fact, not as a subject of the holding.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Trial Term, Oneida County
new.notes: Forcible entry and detainer/treble-damages pleading dispute; plaintiff's status as 'a boarding house keeper' is mentioned only in passing as part of the damages allegation, not adjudicated.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Commercial lot lease/'tenant right' of renewal dispute between horse dealers; no lodging or boarding element.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Certiorari review of an attorney's contempt commitment during a real-estate brokerage trial; retrieval hit is a false positive on broker-commission testimony text, no lodging/boarding content.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Bank receiver's liability for commercial premises rent following a dissolved bank's lease; not a lodging/boarding case.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Nuisance suit against a village for sewage odor damaging a boarding house's rental value; plaintiff's boarding-house business is incidental to the nuisance-damages holding, not about the legality or regulation of letting itself.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Real-estate broker commission dispute discussing constitutionality of a broker-licensing statute (citing the Havnor barber-Sunday-law police-power case); no lodging/boarding content.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Special Term, New York County
new.notes: Specific-performance suit over a deed's use-restriction covenant (distillery, foundry, steam power, etc.); no boarding/lodging restriction or letting arrangement involved.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Ordinary summary dispossession proceeding turning on attornment and a leading-question evidentiary ruling; no lodging/boarding element.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.notes: Summary proceeding procedure/appealability and tenancy-at-will notice requirements; ordinary landlord-tenant dispute unrelated to lodging or boarding.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Special Term, New York County
new.notes: Assignee-of-landlord's right to treat a holdover commercial tenant as renewing for another year; no lodging or boarding element.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Use-and-occupation/adverse-possession dispute among family members residing on land they claimed to inherit; not a paid lodging arrangement.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Injunction against summary dispossession proceedings between purported co-tenant/life-tenant family members with an accounting claim; no lodging or boarding element.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: A hotel employee was convicted of keeping a disorderly house/house of assignation based on two policemen registering with women and being shown to bedrooms; the Appellate Division reversed, holding the evidence insufficient because there was no proof the hotel was a disorderly place, frequented by vicious people, or the site of unlawful doings.

quotes.text: The evidence was insufficient to prove that the hotel was a disorderly house, or house of assignation. There was no evidence that it was a disorderly place, or frequented by disorderly or vicious people, or of any unlawful doings in it.

It is an indictable offense at common law for the keeper of an inn or hotel to refuse to receive any guest and entertain him with meals or lodging or both, and our Penal Code (section 381) makes it a misdemeanor to do so, “without just cause or excuse.”
What was done by the police against this hotel could probably be repeated in the case of most if not all of our hotels, fashionable or plain, high or low.

new.notes: Borderline: this is a criminal disorderly-house/vice prosecution against a licensed hotel rather than a lodging-house licensing case, but the court affirms the innkeeper's ordinary duty/right to receive and lodge paying guests and requires real proof of misconduct before treating a hotel's letting of rooms as unlawful, so flagged favorable to lawful short-term letting for pay.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute over erecting a hospital nurses' residence; 'boarding house' appears only in passing contrast ('neither a flat house, a tenement house, nor a boarding house') describing what the building will NOT be, not a holding on letting or its regulation.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.notes: Property-tax exemption dispute over a college fraternity chapter house that also functioned as a members' boarding place; the boarding arrangement is an internal club-membership fact bearing on the 'exclusive use' tax test, not a letting-to-the-public or lodging-house-regulation question.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Trial Term, Delaware County
new.notes: Perpetual-lease rent/possession action pleaded as breach of covenant rather than ejectment; ordinary land lease dispute, no lodging or boarding element.

new.holding_summary: Denies a preliminary injunction sought by an adjoining landowner to enforce a deed restriction limiting defendant's lot to 'one dwelling house,' for lack of privity of contract/estate and lack of proof the restriction was intended for plaintiff's benefit.
new.notes: Deed building-restriction dispute between adjoining landowners over erection of a factory addition vs. a dwelling house; no lodging, boarding, or compensated occupancy issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: Landlord's boarding-up of a doorway used by a liquor-store tenant constituted an actual eviction from part of the premises, suspending rent; acceptance of back rent after a dispossess warrant did not waive the tenant's eviction defense as to later rent, nor create a month-to-month tenancy.
new.notes: Ordinary commercial (liquor store) landlord-tenant eviction/rent dispute; no lodging or boarding house issue.

new.holding_summary: A 1873 deed covenant forbidding a 'tenement house' is construed in its ordinary popular sense, not per the 1867 statutory definition; modern luxury apartment buildings with private baths, electricity, and elevators do not violate the covenant even though occupied by more than three independent families.
new.notes: Deed-covenant construction of 'tenement house' vs. luxury apartment building; concerns multi-family occupancy classification, not compensated room/lodger letting or boarding-house regulation.

new.holding_summary: A widow with a devisee's interest in partnership real estate who acquiesced in a lease made by the surviving partner is estopped from later disputing its validity; the lessee in possession could not defeat ejectment by acquiring outstanding title from her.
new.notes: Partnership real property lease/ejectment/estoppel dispute; no lodging or boarding-house issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: Evidence that a husband occupied and used property titled to his wife, paying taxes, assessments, and mortgage interest as rent, was sufficient to support finding a landlord-tenant relationship supporting an action for use and occupation; the statute of frauds is no defense once the tenant has entered and occupied under a parol lease longer than a year.
new.notes: Use-and-occupation dispute between spouses over premises used as a livery stable; not a dwelling-letting or lodging/boarding case.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: A contract granting exclusive rights to produce a play permitted the producer to stage it only with its own company, not to sublicense stock theaters to produce it; injunction granted against such sublicensing.
new.notes: Theatrical production/licensing contract dispute; wholly unrelated to real property lodging or boarding-house doctrine.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: A complaint pleading 'use and occupation' at a stated monthly rent, payable in advance, sufficiently alleged an express monthly tenancy; dismissal for supposedly needing to plead an express contract was error.
new.notes: Ordinary monthly house rental/pleading dispute over unpaid rent; tenant occupied continuously for two years, not a short-term lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: A tenant who erected a structure under an oral understanding it would remain his property lost his right to remove it by later accepting new leases that made no reservation of a removal right.
new.notes: Commercial premises fixture-removal dispute (business partnership occupying storefront); no lodging or boarding issue.

new.holding_summary: Overrules a demurrer to a libel complaint concerning a newspaper article about a police raid on plaintiff's boarding house for gambling, holding the article could reasonably be read to imply the plaintiff-keeper's own knowledge of the gambling, distinguishing cases where only the premises (not the individual) were libeled.
new.notes: Plaintiff is described as keeping a private boarding house, but the holding turns entirely on libel-pleading/inference doctrine, not on the legal character or regulation of boarding-house keeping; boarding house is incidental factual backdrop only.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: A deed covenant barring uses that 'injuriously affect' adjoining residence property, coupled with an enumerated list of prohibited business uses, does not bar erection of a building with storerooms merely because store use might incidentally affect neighboring residential value.
new.notes: Deed building-restriction covenant dispute over commercial storefront use; not about lodging/boarding or paying occupants.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: A quarry company exercising due care in blasting to prepare its own land for lawful business use will not be enjoined merely because the incidental jarring disturbs neighboring residences.
new.notes: Nuisance/blasting injunction case; unrelated to lodging or boarding-house doctrine.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: A holographic will was admitted to probate as validly executed under French law because the decedent, though an American citizen, had abandoned his American domicile and established a French domicile before his death; French forced-heirship law limits the legatee to one-fourth of the estate given three surviving legitimate children.
new.notes: Probate/domicile dispute; mentions decedent living in 'hotels and furnished lodgings' only in passing while narrating his travels, not as a doctrinal point about lodging arrangements.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: A subtenant of commercial premises who accepted a new lease from a third party after foreclosure is thereafter estopped from denying that party's title as landlord in a subsequent dispossess proceeding.
new.notes: Commercial subtenancy/estoppel-to-deny-title dispute over storefront premises; no lodging or boarding issue.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: Constructive (not actual physical) possession suffices to maintain a partition action; a claimed tenant by the curtesy may properly be joined as a defendant and the burden of proving a child was born alive rests on the party claiming through that child.
new.notes: Real property partition/inheritance procedure dispute; no letting or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: A restrictive covenant limiting a parcel to 'private dwelling house' use, made for the benefit of the original grantor's retained land, could not be enforced by a remote purchaser of a differently-restricted adjoining parcel because the covenant was never intended for that purchaser's benefit; the court therefore did not reach whether the proposed apartment house violated the covenant.
new.notes: Deed-covenant enforcement (privity/benefit) dispute over apartment-house construction; decided on covenant-benefit grounds without reaching any lodging/boarding characterization.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Division
new.holding_summary: Whether a landlord was negligent in maintaining a common water-closet used by upstairs tenement tenants, whose leakage damaged a ground-floor store tenant's goods, was a jury question; the no-duty-to-repair-demised-premises rule does not bar liability for negligence as to areas retained under the landlord's control.
new.notes: Landlord's-common-area negligence dispute in a mixed store/tenement building; not about the legal character or regulation of letting/lodging.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: Repairs made with the tenant's consent do not constitute an eviction or a surrender of the lease.
new.notes: One-paragraph landlord-tenant eviction/repairs ruling with no facts about lodging or boarding practice.

new.court: New York Supreme Court, Appellate Term
new.holding_summary: A mortgagee who lawfully took possession of leased apartment property from an executor-landlord, and received an assignment of unpaid rent, stood in the conventional landlord relation to the tenant and could bring summary nonpayment proceedings; the tenant, having recognized the executor as landlord, could not challenge the sufficiency of the surrender to the mortgagee.
new.notes: Mortgagee-in-possession/summary-proceedings dispute over leased flat apartments; ordinary landlord-tenant rent collection, not lodging or boarding-house doctrine.

new.notes: Eminent-domain/telephone-conduit dispute over abutting owner's fee in street; no bearing on lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.notes: Fixture-law dispute over a house built on blocks by a vendee's licensee ('suitable for rental as a habitation') on land under executory sale contract; concerns real-vs-personal-property classification of the structure, not the legality or character of letting occupants.
Summary dispossession of stepson from a stable (used as veterinary hospital); tenancy-at-will proof issue unrelated to lodging/boarding.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Fourth Department
new.notes: Municipal police-power dispute over telephone conduit placement in streets; no relation to lodging/boarding.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
new.notes: Action for use-and-occupation rent arising from a sale/resale agreement over a house; a contract-and-agency dispute, not about lodgers or boarding.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Second Department
new.notes: Municipal ordinance requiring streetcar vestibules held beyond city's police power; unrelated to lodging/boarding regulation.
