new.notes: Sanitary Code smoke-nuisance penalty against a brewery under the police power; concerns manufactories, not lodging or boarding houses.

new.court: Supreme Court, Special Term, New York County
new.notes: City land-grant/street-title and wharfage-easement dispute; no relation to lodging or letting of dwellings.

new.court: Supreme Court, Appellate Division, Third Department
new.notes: Tax-redemption case defining 'occupancy' of wild Adirondack land held by a club/inn for purposes of tax-sale notice; occupancy concept is about physical possession of land, not lodger/boarder status.

Will-probate/domicile dispute; decedent's stays in 'furnished lodgings' and a leased furnished house abroad are recited only to establish domicile for testamentary-capacity purposes, not the legal character of letting.
Trade-fixture dispute over an elevator installed by a commercial tenant in a four-story building; no bearing on compensated occupancy or lodging.

Husband's lease of a house for his family; dispute over distress on the wife's goods and exemption law. A cited precedent about furniture liability for a boarding-house keeper's furniture is mentioned only in passing to support an unrelated rule, not at issue in these facts.
Property tax exemption dispute over a church clergy house/rectory; no letting or lodging arrangement with paying occupants.
Municipal milk-and-meat vendor inspection/license ordinance case; unrelated to lodging-house or dwelling regulation despite the adverse-regulation retrieval hit.
Dispute over whether a lease of manufacturing rooms in a factory building was month-to-month or year-to-year; a commercial tenancy, not a dwelling let to lodgers/boarders.
Dispute over dedication and physical width of a public street encroached upon by a fence; no relation to letting of dwellings or rooms.
Private right-of-way easement and swinging-gate dispute between adjoining farm owners; unrelated to lodging or room letting.
Municipal authority to regulate streetcar fares and require transfers; no bearing on residential letting or boarding/lodging houses despite the adverse-regulation retrieval hit.
Landlord-tenant dispute over a rent-acceleration clause triggered by the tenant's removal from a leased house, and distress on a stranger's bailed furniture; not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Dispute over a grantee's right to collect rent after conveyance of leased premises without a formal lease assignment; procedural/technical landlord-tenant question, not a lodging arrangement.
Corporate-law dispute over voting of building-and-loan association stock; the 'incident of ownership' language that triggered retrieval refers to stock-voting rights, not real property letting.
Municipal license-fee dispute over telephone poles and wires under a public-service inspection statute; unrelated to lodging or dwelling regulation.
Dispute between divorced spouses over rents and profits of property held as tenants by entireties; no compensated occupancy by a third-party lodger or boarder.
Malicious prosecution action arising from a debt-collection dispute over goods obtained by false pretenses; unrelated to lodging or room letting.
Store-and-dwelling commercial tenant's trespass claim against his landlord's agent following alleged wrongful eviction for rent default; not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Oral farm-lease dispute with an indemnity agreement against eviction under a paramount title; an agricultural tenancy, not residential lodging.
Farm-lease rent action with a set-off claim for manure and buildings the tenant was barred from removing; agricultural tenancy, not lodging.
Borough license-tax dispute over motor vehicles, held preempted by state motor-vehicle licensing law; unrelated to lodging or dwelling regulation.
Building-restriction/porch encroachment dispute; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Private alley easement/nonuser dispute; unrelated to lodging or letting.
Will construction/ejectment; life tenant's right to 'rent, occupy, or otherwise possess' is passing dicta, not a lodging/boarding dispute.
Party-wall/encroachment dispute; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Commercial saloon-premises lease/abandonment/eviction dispute between landlord and business tenant; not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Mill-race deed exception/trespass dispute; unrelated to lodging or letting.
Set-off between a tort judgment (landlord's wrongful distraint) and a contract judgment for rent; no issue re: character of letting.
Deed exception/road-obstruction dispute; unrelated to lodging or letting.
Building-restriction dispute over a private garage vs. 'stable'; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Ordinary two-year floor lease/repairs dispute between landlord and tenant; not a lodging/boarding arrangement, no regulatory issue.
Municipal parade/assembly permit ordinance struck down as discriminatory class legislation; not lodging-house regulation.
Domicile/desertion maintenance suit; wife's stint 'keeping a rooming house' is a passing biographical detail among several jobs, not the subject of the holding.
Companion case to Commonwealth v. Mervis on parade-permit ordinance; not lodging-house regulation.
Party-wall use/contribution dispute; unrelated to lodging or letting.

Claim for 'boarding' an elderly uncle who lived with nephew's family for decades; turns on family-relation rebuttal of implied promise to pay, not on the legal character of a paid lodging/letting arrangement with a stranger.
Cotenant landlords' rent dispute over a commercial store lease held by partner-tenants; not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Building-restriction dispute over bulk/bay shop windows; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Dwelling-house lease/ejectment/rent-after-termination dispute; ordinary landlord-tenant rent law, not lodging/boarding characterization or regulation.

new.holding_summary: Grantee took title subject to lessor's covenant not to break through a party wall; equity enjoined future violations but denied a mandatory injunction to close the existing opening absent proof of substantial injury.
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute over a party wall between department stores; no lodging/boarding content.

new.holding_summary: A written agreement for the owner to continue residing on her farm while the defendant worked it and shared produce did not establish an ordinary landlord-tenant relationship reserving a 'certain rent,' so the summary repossession statute did not apply.
new.notes: Farm-labor/support agreement between owner and worker; not a dwelling-letting or lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Theater chairs and curtains installed by a lessee were removable trade fixtures, not part of the leasehold, and passed to the sheriff's-sale purchaser of those goods rather than to a later purchaser of the leasehold.
new.notes: Commercial trade-fixture priority dispute over a theater lease; no relation to residential lodging.

new.holding_summary: Land lying within the bed of a laid-out but unopened street remains taxable to its private owner until the city actually opens the street for public use.
new.notes: Municipal tax-exemption dispute over an unopened street; unrelated to lodging.

new.holding_summary: Statutory provisions letting a coal company condemn a neighbor's land for a private tramway and mine entries were unconstitutional, both as outside the act's title and as a taking of private property for private use beyond the police power.
new.notes: Coal-mining eminent-domain/police-power case; no lodging or boarding content.

new.holding_summary: An order refusing all liquor licenses in the county, reciting a full hearing and reasons tied to public necessity, was not shown to be an abuse of the quarter sessions' statutory discretion and was affirmed.
new.notes: Concerns discretion to grant/refuse liquor licenses for inns and taverns; does not address the legal character or regulation of lodging/boarding arrangements themselves.

new.holding_summary: An order granting a retail liquor license after hearing was affirmed where the record showed compliance with statutory procedure and nothing impeached its regularity.
new.notes: Companion liquor-license procedure case; not about lodging-house legal character or regulation.

new.holding_summary: A franchised lighting company could not cut off service to a new owner of commercial premises for a prior tenant's unpaid bill absent actual or constructive notice of a rule requiring payment of arrearages.
new.notes: Utility-service dispute between successive store occupants; no lodging or boarding issue.

new.holding_summary: A city ordinance declaring it a nuisance to keep hogs outside designated districts was a valid police-power measure, even where the plaintiff's piggery predated the surrounding residential development.
new.notes: Municipal nuisance regulation of hog-keeping; unrelated to lodging or letting of rooms.

new.holding_summary: The Fairmount Park Commission's statutory authority to appoint park guards was independent of the city's civil-service acts, so guards appointed without civil-service examination were lawfully employed.
new.notes: Municipal civil-service/park-governance dispute; no relation to lodging.

new.holding_summary: Where a grantor conveyed a lot with the right to build over an adjoining four-foot alley up to the grantor's then building line, the grantee acquired no right to build over a later extension of the alley when the grantor moved his own building forward.
new.notes: Deed/easement boundary dispute over a private alley; no lodging content.

new.holding_summary: An executor's bare power of sale did not authorize him to lease devised real estate for more than three years without the devisees' written authorization, so the leases, and their claimed ratification by acceptance of rent, were void under the Statute of Frauds.
new.notes: Executor's authority to lease commercial office rooms; not a residential lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: A husband's equity bill to enjoin his wife from interfering with his use of land, where she was in possession of the marital home by his original consent, was in substance an ejectment action better resolved at law, so the injunction was reversed.
new.notes: Marital dispute over occupancy of the family home; not a compensated letting/lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: A first-class township's commissioners lacked express or implied statutory authority to enact an ordinance forbidding the feeding of garbage to animals within the township.
new.notes: Township police-power/ordinance-authority case concerning animal feeding; unrelated to lodging.

new.holding_summary: A borough could, in good faith under its police power, refuse to let a franchised electric company plant poles on one particular street while offering a nearby alley instead, notwithstanding its ordinance's general consent to street use.
new.notes: Utility pole-placement/franchise dispute; no relation to lodging or boarding.

new.holding_summary: A judgment for a boarding house guest injured in a stairway fall was reversed for insufficient evidence, since the hallway lights had been extinguished by someone other than the landlord and the plaintiff herself testified there was no hole in the carpet that caused her fall.
new.notes: Negligence suit against a boarding house keeper turning entirely on evidentiary sufficiency; the opinion never addresses the legal character (lease/license/lodging) or regulation of the letting arrangement, only a passing reference to defendant's occupation as boarding house keeper.

new.holding_summary: Where land was conveyed bounded by a private alley that was open and in use at the time of sale, the right to use the alley passed as appurtenant to the grantee absent language excepting it from the grant.
new.notes: Deed-boundary/easement dispute over a private alley; no lodging content.

new.holding_summary: A lease clause giving the tenant 'first privilege' to rent the building for a further three-year term, inserted because the tenant was buying the outgoing tenant's business, entitled him to a three-year extension at the original rent without any change in terms.
new.notes: Commercial storefront lease-renewal dispute; not a residential lodging arrangement.
Dispute over whether a porch structure violates a street-obstruction ordinance; no compensated occupancy or lodging issue.
Criminal forcible-entry-and-detainer dispute over possession of a farm; no letting-for-pay or lodging issue.
Breach-of-covenant suit over a defective party wall violating building code; no lodging or short-term letting involved.
Board of Health nuisance-abatement case concerning a piggery; retrieved on generic police-power language, not lodging/boarding regulation.
Agricultural way-going-crop dispute between farm landlord and tenant; no compensated room/dwelling letting at issue.
Ordinary written-lease rent/holding-over dispute for a full dwelling; not a lodging, boarding, or short-term room-letting arrangement.
Fire-insurance coverage dispute turning on vacancy of a farm dwelling and ownership; no letting/lodging for pay involved.
Divorce/adultery evidence case; a rooming house is mentioned only in passing as the site of a visit, not litigated as a lodging arrangement.

Sublease/eviction dispute over removal of fixtures (sink, lavatory, blinds) between office subtenant and sublessor; 'housekeeping apartments' mentioned only as background, not litigated for lodging character.
Estate claim for back rent against a relative who occupied a house gratuitously as an act of family kindness; no compensated letting arrangement existed.
Replevin action over distraint for rent turning on entireties ownership and to whom rent is properly paid; not about lodging or short-term letting.
Injunction enforcing a deed building-restriction against a garage; no letting or lodging issue.
Police-power/ordinance-reasonableness case about gasoline storage limits; retrieved on generic police-power language, unrelated to lodging houses.
Negligence suit over a defective coal-hole cover on a leased commercial sidewalk; landlord/tenant repair-liability doctrine, not lodging.
Ground-rent/federal income tax allocation dispute; no dwelling letting or lodging issue.
Fire-insurance dispute over vacancy and sole-ownership of a residence; tenant occupancy mentioned only incidentally, not lodging/boarding.
Wrongful-distress replevin turning on termination of a lease made by a life tenant at her death; no lodging/short-term letting issue.

Criminal case on leasing a house for prostitution disguised as an installment sale, evading an anti-bawdy-house statute; regulates vice, not the household lodging/boarding-house practice at issue in this study.
Farm lease dispute over custom regarding division of hay; no dwelling/lodging letting.
Easement/water-rights dispute over a mill race obstruction; no dwelling letting.
Building-restriction covenant dispute over a street railway loop encroaching on a setback; no dwelling occupancy for pay.

new.holding_summary: A householder who lets two rooms of his dwelling to tenants is treated under ordinary landlord-tenant law, and in the absence of fraud or concealment is not liable to the tenant for injuries from a defect existing at the time of the demise. The rule of caveat emptor applies in full force, requiring the tenant to use ordinary care to discover open defects, including those in shared means of ingress/egress.

quotes.text: October 5, 1914, plaintiffs leased two rooms on the third floor of defendant’s house, and had lived in the premises five days when an accident occurred.

In the absence of fraud or concealment a landlord is not responsible for injuries resulting from defects existing at the time of the demise: 16 Ruling Case LaAV, p. 1059; Borggard v. Gale, 205 Ill. 511. The rule of caveat emptor applies in full force and the tenant and his family are bound to use their eyes to discover such defects as are open to observation or inspection: 24 Cyc. 1114.
The rule of caveat emptor applies in full force and the tenant and his family are bound to use their eyes to discover such defects as are open to observation or inspection

new.notes: Landlord let two rooms of his own house to a tenant family sharing a common drying platform with other occupants; court applies ordinary lease/caveat-emptor doctrine without special disability, treating the room-letting as an ordinary incident of ownership. Exact lease term not stated (only that plaintiffs had occupied five days at time of accident).
Building-line/porch-enclosure covenant dispute between neighboring homeowners; no compensated occupancy at issue.

Liquor-license refusal case; hotel's need for food/lodging accommodation is mentioned only to distinguish it from the separate question of liquor-license necessity. Does not adjudicate the legality or regulation of the lodging/hotel business itself.
Commercial-premises lease dispute (notice to quit, waiver of forfeiture, distress for rent) between a landlord and an assignee of a business lease; not a dwelling/lodging letting.
Oil lease royalty dispute (executor's power to lease land for oil); unrelated to dwelling occupancy.
Police-power licensing case for junk dealers; not lodging/boarding-house regulation.

new.holding_summary: A divorce libellant could not establish legal Pennsylvania residence merely by showing he rented a room in a Philadelphia rooming house for $15 a month and stayed there on average two nights a week, while paying no local taxes, voting nowhere, having no Pennsylvania business, and keeping his family ties in New Jersey. The court treated his occasional, temporary rooming-house stays as legally insufficient to establish a true, fixed, permanent residence.

quotes.text: the husband, who is thirty-eight years of age, rented a room in a rooming house in Philadelphia, in April, 1915, for the sum of $15 a month, which was later reduced to $12.

A libellant in divorce cannot establish the fact of a legal residence in Pennsylvania, by proof that he rented a room in a rooming house in Philadelphia for the sum of fifteen dollars a month, that he spent on an average at least two nights a week at the house during the year
His irregular occasional and temporary stay in the Philadelphia boarding house shows the lack of all the essential elements in establishing a true, fixed, permanent residence.

new.notes: Not a case adjudicating the legality of room-letting itself; it uses the paid rooming-house stay as evidence that occupant lacked a bona fide domicile. Included because the court squarely characterizes the legal nature of a paid rooming-house stay (transient, not residence) — polarity marked mixed as it neither validates nor restricts the letting practice, but treats lodger occupancy as legally lesser than tenancy/domicile.
Dedication-of-alley dispute involving a market house's stall space; commercial market stalls, not dwelling lodging.
Street-railway traffic-direction ordinance case; police power over street traffic, unrelated to dwelling letting.
Deed-boundary dispute over use of a private alley; no dwelling occupancy for pay.
Billboard-licensing police-power case; not lodging/boarding-house regulation.
Procedural landlord-tenant statute case (affidavit sufficiency to remove summary-possession proceeding to Common Pleas); no substantive discussion of dwelling letting practice.
Guardian's-sale/alley-dedication dispute over a rear alley appurtenant to a lot; no dwelling letting for pay.
Autobus route-regulation ordinance case; police power over motor carriers, unrelated to dwelling letting.
Divorce indignities case; couple lived together in their own household/apartment 'doing light housekeeping' and with family, no paid lodging or boarding arrangement described.
Alley easement/servitude dispute between neighboring landowners over an implied reservation and a gate; no occupancy-for-pay or lodging issue.

Amicable ejectment for nonpayment of rent under a written lease to a married woman; opinion addresses her capacity to contract and notice-of-quit procedure, not the character or short-term nature of the letting.
Trust accounting dispute over whether proceeds from a stock-subscription right belong to corpus or life-tenant income; wholly unrelated to dwelling letting.
Pleading-sufficiency dispute in a replevin action arising from a landlord's distress for rent on household goods; addresses procedure only, not the nature of the tenancy or letting.
Dispute over rentals and free-gas clause under an oil-and-gas lease and the location of a well relative to a boundary; not a dwelling/room letting case.

Divorce case turning on bona fide domicile; libellant's successive stays in lodging/rooming houses (weekly-paid rooms) are recited only to test residency, and the court never adjudicates the legal character of the lodging arrangements themselves.
Landlord-tenant ejectment proceeding resolved on a parol exchange-of-farmland defense and cross-examination scope; no short-term/lodging letting issue.
Conspiracy-to-defraud prosecution against private detectives; defendant's rooming house is mentioned only as the site of alleged misconduct and is not itself adjudicated.

Tenant's negligence suit against landlord/trustee for injury on a shared roof platform used by all six tenants of a house to hang laundry; decides the landlord's tort duty to maintain common areas, not the legal character or regulation of the letting.

Drug-possession prosecution turning on search-and-seizure and after-discovered evidence; defendant's status as a rooming-house proprietress and her claim the drugs were a boarder's are incidental facts, not adjudicated.
Equity suit over building-line restrictions and conversion of porch space into a private garage; no room/dwelling letting issue.
Landlord-tenant covenant-breach case over a subtenant's unauthorized alterations to a subleased structure; concerns covenant/subletting enforcement, not the character of short-term dwelling letting.
Board-of-health ordinance prohibiting slaughterhouses held ultra vires; a police-power regulation case but concerns slaughterhouses, not lodging/boarding houses.

Pandering/transportation prosecution reversed for insufficient evidence; the newly opened lodging house where the complainant was placed is mentioned in passing and its letting arrangement is never adjudicated.
Party-wall compensation dispute under the 1721 Act; unrelated to letting of rooms or dwellings.

Divorce-desertion case affirming dismissal; the court's dictum that many people are 'compelled to live in furnished rooms' addresses whether the wife's refusal to join her husband was justified, not the legal character of any letting.
Ejectment action turning on proof standards for title by adverse possession; no letting-for-pay issue.
Boundary/ejectment dispute over a garage's encroachment and its footing course; unrelated to dwelling letting.

new.holding_summary: Equity dispute between adjoining landowners over dedication and obstruction of a private alley; injunction against obstruction affirmed.
new.notes: Property boundary/easement dispute; no letting or lodging issue.

new.holding_summary: Divorce decree reversed where evidence of wife's desertion was fabricated and record instead showed husband's own desertions.
new.notes: Mentions husband renting furnished rooms for his wife/daughter as an incidental fact in a desertion case; not litigation over letting practice itself.

new.holding_summary: Borough lacked statutory authority to license motor vehicles carrying passengers for hire; such power suspended by state Motor Vehicle Act.
new.notes: Motor carrier licensing case, unrelated to lodging/letting of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: Divorce decree for desertion reversed on appeal; mere silence of complainant does not establish mutual consent to separation.
new.notes: Couple's occupancy of rooms in a rooming-house is incidental background to a desertion claim, not an adjudicated lodging/letting issue.

new.holding_summary: Private garage found to be a nuisance interfering with neighbor's use of her home; removal order (available only to municipality) struck, damages award vacated for insufficient proof.
new.notes: Garage-as-nuisance/zoning case; no letting of rooms or dwelling for pay.

new.holding_summary: Commercial store lease's acceleration clause triggered by receivership; landlord entitled to preferred claim for one year's rent under 1919 Act, remainder as general creditor.
new.notes: Commercial storeroom lease/receivership priority dispute, not residential lodging.

new.holding_summary: Zoning Board of Appeals erred in permitting enclosure of a porch as a garage absent findings of practical difficulty or unnecessary hardship.
new.notes: Zoning variance procedure for a garage addition; unrelated to lodging/letting.

new.holding_summary: Injunction sustained against occupying a garage as a residence in violation of a deed restriction requiring a two-story dwelling costing at least $2,500.
new.notes: Restrictive-covenant enforcement re: garage-as-residence; no letting for pay at issue.

new.holding_summary: Summary judgment reversed in dispute over buyer's right to inspect potatoes shipped f.o.b. before accepting/rejecting a produce contract.
new.notes: Sale-of-goods contract dispute; wholly unrelated to lodging or dwelling occupancy.

new.holding_summary: Leasing garage space exclusively to an apartment house's own tenants for car storage is a private, not public, garage use, so contempt order for violating injunction against public-garage use reversed.
new.notes: Public-vs-private garage nuisance/injunction case involving apartment tenants; no bearing on letting rooms/dwellings for pay.

new.holding_summary: Will construction case; devise of two houses 'to collect the rents...as long as she shall live' held to pass a fee simple, not a life estate.
new.notes: Testamentary construction/estates case; rent-collection language is about ownership incidents, not lodging practice.

new.holding_summary: Fire insurance policy upheld for plaintiff where no evidence landlord knew of or controlled tenant's operation of an illegal still that increased fire hazard.
new.notes: Insurance/landlord-tenant hazard-increase dispute; tenancy is incidental to the insurance question, not about lodging/letting doctrine.

new.holding_summary: North Carolina juvenile court custody decree entitled to full faith and credit; children ordered returned to North Carolina custody (majority opinion), with a dissent urging a best-interests rehearing.
new.notes: Child-custody/full-faith-and-credit case; 'boarding house keeper' is merely the custodian's occupation, not a litigated lodging arrangement.

new.holding_summary: Husband's divorce action for desertion denied; wife's departure from husband's parents' home was legally justified and husband acquiesced in the separation.
new.notes: Wife's proposal to get furnished rooms is a hypothetical living arrangement mentioned in a desertion case, not an adjudicated letting issue.

new.holding_summary: Default judgment against landlord for failure to repair set aside because no cause of action was stated; landlord has no duty to repair absent an express lease covenant.
new.notes: Ordinary landlord repair-duty/negligence pleading case; not about the character or regulation of short-term letting.

new.holding_summary: Landlord's summary possession judgment for nonpayment of rent reversed on demurrer because the statement of claim omitted facts essential under the 1830 Act.
new.notes: Procedural pleading dispute over a commercial premises lease ($2,000/year); not lodging/boarding.

new.holding_summary: Tax assessment case holding that under the 1842 Act a farm split by borough lines is assessed where the mansion house sits, though a separate dwelling in exclusive occupancy of the owner's mother and sister (rent-free) is separately assessable in the borough.
new.notes: Property tax-assessment/mansion-house doctrine case; family rent-free occupancy is discussed for tax severance purposes, not short-term paid lodging.

new.holding_summary: Cotenant in sole possession of jointly-owned property owes no accounting to cotenants for use and occupation absent an express agreement, ouster, or rents received from third parties.
new.notes: Tenants-in-common accounting dispute over inherited property; no third-party lodging/letting involved.
Commercial lease of storerooms/dwelling for a grocery and liquor business; dispute is about eviction and damages, not compensated lodging/boarding.
Licensing of the undertaking business under police power; unrelated to lodging or boarding houses.
Ground rent title/presumption dispute arising from a break in the chain of conveyances; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Municipal license fee on a water company for opening streets to repair mains; no connection to residential lodging.
Ordinary commercial lease renewal-notice covenant and holding-over dispute; not a lodging/boarding case.
Trade-fixture ownership dispute in a leased drug store; no lodging/boarding issue.
License tax on telegraph poles/wires under police power; unrelated to residential letting or boarding.
Partition action between tenants in common; decedent lived with defendant in one of the co-owned houses, but this is incidental to a title/adverse-possession dispute, not compensated occupancy.
Deed exception/reservation of a graveyard vs. railroad ejectment; no occupancy-for-pay issue.
Treble-damages statute for quarrying stone on another's land; no connection to lodging or boarding.

quotes.text: provided, nevertheless, and with the express condition that she, the said Emma Lehder, shall or will not let or sublet any part of it, except for the purpose of keeping boarders or roomers; and such boarders or roomers to be only such people whose character and reputation are above reproach, for the purpose of keeping said children in good, healthy and moral surroundings.

new.notes: Keeping boarders/roomers appears only as a permitted-use condition recited from the articles of separation; the court's actual holding concerns assignee-for-creditors title/notice, not the legal character of the boarding arrangement, so characterization is left null.
Building-restriction covenant and injunction against a carriage-house encroachment; no lodging/boarding issue.
Res judicata dispute over rent owed by a surety under an ordinary residential house lease (Mrs. Quinn as tenant); not a lodging/boarding arrangement.
Municipal ordinance against casting handbills/circulars into vestibules; not a lodging-house regulation.
Commercial store lease holding-over dispute; not a lodging/boarding case.
Ejectment turning on adverse possession and tenancy-imputation between family members/heirs; not compensated lodging.
Building-restriction/window-covenant dispute between adjoining owners; no lodging/boarding issue.
Landlord's distress on consigned shoe-store goods; commercial retail tenancy, not lodging/boarding.

new.holding_summary: Municipal sewer-lien dispute over whether a street was validly dedicated to public use; has nothing to do with letting dwellings or rooms.
new.notes: Deed-dedication/street-easement case; no occupancy-for-pay issue at all.

new.holding_summary: Trespass action after ejectment execution; sister's possession was as her brother's housekeeper, not as a lodger or tenant paying for occupancy.
new.notes: Family occupancy/housekeeping arrangement incident to ejectment execution, not a compensated letting.

new.holding_summary: Upholds a borough peddler/canvasser licensing ordinance under the police power, but strikes down its exemption clause as an unreasonable classification; concerns door-to-door sales, not lodging or dwelling rentals.
new.notes: Peddler/hawker licensing ordinance case; no boarding-house or lodging-house regulation or letting of premises involved.

new.holding_summary: Procedural ruling on the sufficiency of an answer to a rule to bring ejectment against a life tenant's remainderman; no occupancy-for-pay facts.
new.notes: Life estate/remainder title dispute; unrelated to short-term letting or lodging.

new.holding_summary: Upholds constitutionality of a statute licensing junk shops and second-hand dealers under the police power; not itself about lodging houses or letting dwellings.
new.notes: In passing, the opinion cites Commonwealth v. Muir (1 Pa. Superior Ct. 579; aff'd 180 Pa. 47) as precedent that an act licensing public lodging houses was constitutional, but Mintz itself adjudicates junk-dealer licensing, not lodging. Muir may be worth pulling directly as an adverse-regulation candidate in a later shard, but this record does not qualify on its own facts.

new.holding_summary: Construes a commercial lease's renewal/rerenting privilege for two rooms in a building, holding the tenant exhausted his renewal right by giving notice of only a one-year extension.
new.notes: Ordinary annual commercial lease-renewal dispute (two rooms let at $125/year); no short-term or lodging character, no householder letting part of a residence.

new.holding_summary: Holds a landlord liable in negligence to one of several separately-leased tenants for injuries from a defective common stairway he was bound to maintain.
new.notes: Multi-tenant building with separate room leases, but the opinion addresses only the landlord's premises-liability duty over common stairways, not the character or duration of the lettings themselves — no lease/license/lodging characterization at issue.

new.holding_summary: Farm-tenancy dispute over entitlement to a way-going crop under a written lease versus local custom; agricultural, not residential/lodging letting.
new.notes: Farm lease/crop-share dispute; no bearing on letting rooms or dwellings.

new.holding_summary: Voids a Pittsburgh smoke-nuisance ordinance provision as unreasonable; concerns industrial smoke abatement under the police power, not lodging or dwelling regulation.
new.notes: Smoke-nuisance ordinance case; unrelated to letting or lodging.
Curbstone-market ordinance dispute over a farmer selling produce on the street; no letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging-house regulation.
Wrongful-distress damages dispute between landlord and tenant; concerns distraint remedies only, not the character or duration of any letting.
Dispute over withdrawal of a notice to quit and renewal of an ordinary year-to-year house lease; no lodger/boarder occupancy at issue.
Dispute over a revoked municipal permit to erect a street reviewing stand; no dwelling-letting or lodging-house regulation involved.
Replevin action over distraint of a stranger's goods found on the sidewalk of demised premises; house was leased as a whole, no lodger/boarder facts at issue.
Parol lease of a brickyard for commercial brick manufacture, dispute over tenancy-at-will vs. year-to-year status and eviction; no dwelling-lodging occupancy.
Farm lease dispute over cattle deaths allegedly caused by oil-drilling operations under a reserved mineral-lease clause; no dwelling/lodging occupancy at issue.
Borough ordinance requiring a railroad to station a watchman at a grade crossing; a police-power case but not about lodging/boarding houses or dwelling-letting.
Liquor-license refusal based on a restrictive covenant in the deed against sale of liquor on the premises; unrelated to letting rooms/dwellings or lodging-house regulation.

Decedent was an 18-day boarder in defendant's boarding house, but the holding is pure gift-inter-vivos delivery doctrine (validity of a note given by the boarder to the boarding-house keeper); the boarding relationship is incidental background, not doctrinally characterized.
Deed-reservation/alley dispute over right to maintain a building above an alley, plus married-woman estoppel; no letting, lodging, or boarding content.

new.holding_summary: A landlord executing on a judgment for rent cannot levy on and sell the goods of a stranger found on the demised premises; a new legal principle may be raised on a motion for judgment n.o.v. even if not argued at trial.
new.notes: Landlord-tenant execution/distress dispute over a leased soda fountain (chattel of a stranger); no bearing on letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging regulation.

new.holding_summary: A landlord whose land is in a tenant's exclusive possession may still maintain trespass against a telephone company for injury to the reversion, such as destruction of trees.
new.notes: Trespass/reversion dispute involving farmland and a telephone line; tenancy mentioned only to establish standing to sue, no bearing on letting of rooms or lodging.

new.holding_summary: A surety who bonded a tenant's distrained household goods remained liable on the bond notwithstanding a bankruptcy trustee's disclaimer of other distrained property (hearses/casket wagon) held by the tenant as bailee.
new.notes: Landlord distress for rent, surety bond, and bailment of business chattels; no bearing on letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging.

new.holding_summary: A covenant in leases of company-owned dwelling houses restricting use of the private access way to ingress/egress did not bar delivery of goods ordered by tenants, but did bar use of the way to solicit orders from other tenants once posted under the Act of 1905.
new.notes: Leased company dwelling houses and private-way access covenant/posted-land trespass; tenants are ordinary lessees of company houses, not lodgers/boarders, and the dispute is about the way, not the letting itself.

new.holding_summary: The orphans' court had jurisdiction over a tenant-by-curtesy's partition petition; adverse possession claimed by cotenants was insufficient to bar partition, and an inquest's unequal-value allotment was set aside.
new.notes: Estate partition and tenancy-by-curtesy dispute; unrelated to letting of rooms/dwellings or lodging regulation.

new.holding_summary: Where a licensee built a boundary wall that mistakenly encroached beyond the licensed line, equity ordered the wall relocated to the agreed line rather than wholly removed and rebuilt.

new.holding_summary: Where a real estate broker's employment was non-exclusive and commissions were conditioned on procuring a signed lease and down payment, the broker was not entitled to commission merely for bringing landlord and prospective tenant together.
new.notes: Broker-commission dispute over a five-year commercial lease of storefront premises to an ice cream company; commercial letting, not householder short-term room/lodging letting.

new.notes: Bailment/consignment of watch cases in a creditor's interpleader action; unrelated to occupancy of dwellings.

new.holding_summary: A borough ordinance requiring a license fee for hawkers, peddlers, and house-to-house solicitors was a reasonable and valid exercise of the police power, not a prohibitory measure.
new.notes: Peddler/hawker licensing case; regulates itinerant selling, not lodging or boarding houses.

new.holding_summary: A testamentary devise in fee simple could not be validly restricted by a condition against alienation except by will, or against liability for the devisee's debts; such conditions are void as repugnant to the fee.

new.holding_summary: In ejectment, evidence that defendant entered farmland under a parol gift, cleared and improved it, and paid taxes for over thirty years was sufficient to submit adverse possession to the jury, including constructive possession of the whole tract through a tenant occupying part of it.

That liability extended to the plaintiff, a lodger who had rented a room in the house from the landlord's tenant and was hurt by the defect returning home at night. The court affirmed a jury verdict for the injured lodger against the property owner.

new.holding_summary: A former domestic servant claimed against the estate of a woman of means for over three years of boarding and nursing furnished in the servant's own home. The court disallowed the claim, holding that boarding and nursing services, like domestic wages, are presumed to be paid at stated periods, and the claimant failed to produce evidence rebutting that presumption despite the decedent's ample means and habit of paying bills promptly.
